title.zh: 卷二百九十九 列傳第五十八 狄棐 郎簡 孫祖德 張若谷 石揚休 祖士衡 李垂 張洞 李仕衡 李溥 胡則 薛顏 許元 鍾離瑾 孫沖 崔嶧 田瑜 施昌言
title.en: Volume 299 Biographies 58: Di Fei, Lang Jian, Sun Zude, Zhang Ruogu, Shi Yangxiu, Zu Shiheng, Li Chui, Zhang Dong, Li Shiheng, Li Pu, Hu Ze, Xue Yan, Xu Yuan, Zhong Lijin, Sun Chong, Cui Yi, Tian Yu, Shi Changyan
title.raw: 卷二百九十九 列傳第五十八 狄棐 郎簡 孫祖德 張若谷 石揚休 祖士衡 李垂 張洞 李仕衡 李溥 胡則 薛顏 許元 鍾離瑾 孫沖 崔嶧 田瑜 施昌言 Volume 299 Biographies 58: Di Fei, Lang Jian, Sun Zude, Zhang Ruogu, Shi Yangxiu, Zu Shiheng, Li Chui, Zhang Dong, Li Shiheng, Li Pu, Hu Ze, Xue Yan, Xu Yuan, Zhong Lijin, Sun Chong, Cui Yi, Tian Yu, Shi Changyan

sentences.zh: 狄棐，字輔之，潭州長沙人。

translations.literal: Di Fei, styled Fuzhi, was a native of Changsha in Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Di Fei, courtesy name Fuzhi, came from Changsha in Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 少隨父官徐州，以文謁路振，振器愛之，妻以女。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his father to an official post in Xuzhou; presenting literary compositions to Lu Zhen, Zhen greatly admired him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he accompanied his father to a post in Xuzhou, presented his writings to Lu Zhen, and won such favor that Zhen married him to his daughter.

sentences.zh: 舉進士甲科，以大理評事知分宜縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the top grade and was appointed as a reviewing officer in the Court of Judicial Review to serve as magistrate of Fenyi County.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in the highest class and was made a judicial reviewer with appointment as magistrate of Fenyi County.

sentences.zh: 歷開封府司錄，知壁州。

translations.literal: He successively served as recorder of the Kaifeng prefectural government and as prefect of Bizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as recorder of Kaifeng prefecture and as prefect of Bizhou.

sentences.zh: 道長安，為寇準所厚，準復入相，乃薦通判益州。

translations.literal: Passing through Chang'an, he won the esteem of Kou Zhun; when Kou again entered the council as chief minister, he recommended Fei as assistant prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: While traveling through Chang'an he impressed Kou Zhun, and when Kou returned to the chief ministership he recommended Fei as vice-prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 擢開封府判官，歷京西益州路轉運、江淮制置發運使，累遷太常少卿、知廣州，加直昭文館。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice-director of the Kaifeng prefecture, served as transport commissioner on the Jingxi and Yizhou circuits and as salt distribution commissioner for the Jiang-Huai region, and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Guangzhou, with concurrent appointment as a scholar of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice-director of Kaifeng, held transport posts on the Jingxi and Yizhou circuits and the Jiang-Huai salt commission, and was promoted repeatedly to Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Guangzhou, with a concurrent post in the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 代還，不以南海物自隨，人稱其廉。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, he did not bring South Sea goods with him; people praised his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from his tour of duty he took no goods from the southern seas with him, and people praised his probity.

sentences.zh: 拜右諫議大夫、龍圖閣直學士、權判吏部流內銓，出知滑州，進給事中，徙天雄軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Remonstrance Official, Academician in the Dragon Diagram Hall, and acting director of the Bureau of Personnel Rosters in the Ministry of Personnel; he went out to serve as prefect of Huazhou, was promoted to Drafting Official, and was transferred to the Tianxiong army command.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Remonstrance Official and Academician in the Dragon Diagram Hall, acting head of the Ministry roster bureau, then sent out as prefect of Huazhou, promoted to Drafting Official, and transferred to the Tianxiong command.

sentences.zh: 會給郊賞帛不善，士卒譁譟趣府門，棐不能治。

translations.literal: When the suburban sacrificial rewards of silk were found to be poor in quality, the troops clamored and rushed to the government gate; Fei could not suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When the silk given as suburban sacrificial rewards proved shoddy, the soldiers clamored and surged to the government gate, and Fei could not bring them under control.

sentences.zh: 事聞，命侍御史劉夔按視，未及境，眾不自安。

translations.literal: The matter was reported; the emperor ordered Investigating Censor Liu Kui to inspect the case. Before Liu reached the border, the crowd grew uneasy on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached the throne, and the emperor ordered Investigating Censor Liu Kui to look into it; before Liu crossed into the region the men had already grown restless on their own.

sentences.zh: 棐馳白夔，請紿以行河事。

translations.literal: Fei rode posthaste to inform Liu, asking him to deceive them by saying he was going on river business.
translations.idiomatic: Fei galloped ahead to tell Liu to deceive the troops by saying he had come on river-control business.

sentences.zh: 夔至，與轉運使李絳誅首惡數人。

translations.literal: When Liu arrived, he and Transport Commissioner Li Jiang executed several ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu arrived, he and Transport Commissioner Li Jiang put several ringleaders to death.

sentences.zh: 棐坐罷懦，降知隨州，徙同州。

translations.literal: Fei was punished for cowardice and demoted to prefect of Suizhou, then transferred to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fei was found guilty of timidity, demoted to prefect of Suizhou, and later transferred to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 勾當三班院，進樞密直學士，歷知陝鄭州、河中河南府，復判流內銓。

translations.literal: He oversaw the Third-Rank Bureau, was promoted to Academician in the Council of State, successively served as prefect of Shaan and Zhengzhou and of Hezhong and Henan prefectures, and again served as director of the Bureau of Personnel Rosters.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the Third-Rank Bureau, was promoted to Academician in the Council of State, served in turn as prefect of Shaan and Zhengzhou and of Hezhong and Henan, and again headed the roster bureau.

sentences.zh: 出知揚州，未行，卒。

translations.literal: He was sent out to serve as prefect of Yangzhou; before he could take up the post, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Yangzhou but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 有狄國賓者，仁傑之後，分仁傑告身與棐，棐奏錄國賓一官，而自稱仁傑十四世孫。

translations.literal: There was one Di Guobin, a descendant of Di Renjie, who divided Renjie's certificate of appointment and gave part to Fei; Fei memorialized to register Guobin for one official rank and himself claimed to be Renjie's fourteenth-generation descendant.
translations.idiomatic: A certain Di Guobin, a descendant of Di Renjie, shared Renjie's commission document with Fei; Fei memorialized to grant Guobin an office and himself styled Renjie's fourteenth-generation descendant.

sentences.zh: 棐在河中時，有中貴人過郡，言將援棐於上前。

translations.literal: When Fei was in Hezhong, an important eunuch passed through the prefecture and said he would speak for Fei at court.
translations.idiomatic: While Fei was prefect of Hezhong, a senior eunuch passing through the prefecture said he would put in a word for him at court.

sentences.zh: 棐答以他語，退謂所親曰：「吾湘潭一寒士，今官侍從，可以老而自汙耶？」

translations.literal: Fei answered with other words; retiring he said to those close to him: "I am but a poor scholar of Xiangtan; today I hold a court attendant's office—can I disgrace myself in old age?"
translations.idiomatic: Fei replied evasively, then withdrew and told his intimates, "I was only a poor scholar from Xiangtan; now I am a court attendant—should I stain my old age?"

sentences.zh: 其為政愷悌，不為表襮，死之日，家無餘貲。

translations.literal: In his conduct in office he was kind and easygoing; he did not put on a show. On the day of his death his household had no surplus funds.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with kindness and ease and never made a display of virtue; when he died his family had nothing left over.

sentences.zh: 子 遵度

translations.literal: Son: Zundu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zundu

sentences.zh: 子遵度，字元規。

translations.literal: His son Zundu, styled Yuangui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zundu, courtesy name Yuangui.

sentences.zh: 少穎悟，篤志於學。

translations.literal: From youth he was quick-witted and single-minded in study.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was clever and wholly devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 每讀書，意有所得，即仰屋瞪視，人呼之，弗聞也。

translations.literal: Whenever he read, if an idea came to him he would stare up at the ceiling; people might call him but he would not hear.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he read and grasped an idea he would stare up at the rafters; people could call him and he would not hear.

sentences.zh: 少舉進士，一斥於有司，恥不復為。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in his youth; once rejected by the authorities, he was shamed and never tried again.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi while young; after the authorities rejected him once he was too ashamed to try again.

sentences.zh: 以父任為襄縣主簿，居數月，棄去。

translations.literal: Through his father's position he was appointed registrar of Xiang County; after several months he abandoned the post.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through his father's privilege as registrar of Xiang County, but after a few months he quit.

sentences.zh: 好為古文，著《春秋雜說》，多所發明。

translations.literal: He loved writing ancient-style prose and authored Miscellaneous Discourses on the Spring and Autumn, with many original insights.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in ancient-style prose and wrote Miscellaneous Discourses on the Spring and Autumn Annals, with many fresh points.

sentences.zh: 嘗患時學靡敝，作《擬皇太子冊文》、《除侍御史制》、《裴晉公傳》，人多稱之。

translations.literal: He once grieved that learning of the age had declined and composed "Imitation Enthronement Document for the Crown Prince," "Edict Appointing a Palace Censor," and "Biography of Pei Jinggong," for which many praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Once, lamenting the decay of learning in his day, he wrote an imitation enthronement document for the crown prince, an edict appointing a palace censor, and a biography of Pei Jinggong, all widely praised.

sentences.zh: 尤嗜杜甫詩，賞讚其集。

translations.literal: He was especially fond of Du Fu's poetry and praised his collected works.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially devoted to Du Fu's poetry and commended his collected poems.

sentences.zh: 一夕，夢見甫為誦世所未見詩，及覺，才記十餘字，遵度足成之，為《佳城篇》。

translations.literal: One night he dreamed that Fu was reciting for him a poem never seen in the world; when he awoke he could remember only a dozen-odd characters; Zundu completed it into "The Fine City."
translations.idiomatic: One night he dreamed Du Fu reciting a poem unknown in the world; on waking he recalled only a dozen or so characters, and Zundu finished it as "The Fine City."

sentences.zh: 後數月卒。

translations.literal: Several months later he died.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he died.

sentences.zh: 有集十二卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twelve fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to twelve fascicles.

sentences.zh: 郎簡，字叔廉，杭州臨安人。

translations.literal: Lang Jian, styled Shulian, was a native of Lin'an in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Jian, courtesy name Shulian, was from Lin'an in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼孤貧，借書錄之，多至成誦。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor in youth, he borrowed books and copied them out, often memorizing them whole.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor as a boy, he borrowed books and copied them, often learning them by heart entire.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，補試秘書省校書郎、知寧國縣，徙福清令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed after examination as proofreader in the Secretariat and magistrate of Ningguo County; he was transferred to be magistrate of Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi, was made a proofreader in the Secretariat after examination, and served as magistrate of Ningguo and then Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 縣有石塘陂，歲久湮塞，募民浚築，溉廢田百餘頃，邑人為立生祠。

translations.literal: The county had the Shitang embankment, long silted up; he recruited the people to dredge and build it, irrigating over a hundred mu of abandoned fields; the county people erected a living shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: The county's Shitang reservoir had long silted over; he raised labor to dredge and rebuild it, bringing more than a hundred mu of fallow land under irrigation, and the people set up a living shrine to him.

sentences.zh: 調隨州推官，及引對，真宗曰：「簡歷官無過，而無一人薦，是必恬於進者。」

translations.literal: He was transferred to be judicial assistant in Suizhou; at his audience Emperor Zhenzong said: "Jian has never had fault in any post, yet not one person has recommended him—he must be one who is content not to advance."
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to judicial assistant in Suizhou, at his audience Zhenzong said, "Jian has never erred in office, yet no one has recommended him—he must be content to stay out of the scramble for promotion."

sentences.zh: 特改秘書省著作佐郎、知分宜縣，徙知竇州。

translations.literal: He was specially changed to Assistant Compiler in the Secretariat and magistrate of Fenyi County, then transferred to be prefect of Baozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially made an assistant compiler in the Secretariat and magistrate of Fenyi, then transferred to prefect of Baozhou.

sentences.zh: 縣吏死，子幼，贅婿偽為券冒有其貲。

translations.literal: A county clerk died leaving an infant son; a son-in-law living in the household forged a deed and seized the property.
translations.idiomatic: A county clerk died leaving a young son; a son-in-law who had married into the family forged a deed and seized the estate.

sentences.zh: 及子長，屢訴不得直，乃訟於朝。

translations.literal: When the son grew up he sued repeatedly but could not obtain justice, and finally lodged suit at court.
translations.idiomatic: When the son came of age he sued again and again without redress and finally appealed to the capital.

sentences.zh: 下簡劾治，簡示以舊牘曰：「此爾翁書耶？」

translations.literal: The case was sent down to Jian for investigation; Jian showed him the old documents and said: "Is this your father's hand?"
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to Jian; he showed the old papers and asked, "Is this your father's writing?"

translations.literal: He said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: The man said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 又取偽券示之，弗類也，始伏罪。

translations.literal: Jian again showed him the forged deed; it did not match, and only then did he confess.
translations.idiomatic: Jian then produced the forged deed; it did not match, and the man confessed at last.

sentences.zh: 徙藤州，興學養士，一變其俗，藤自是始有舉進士者。

translations.literal: Transferred to Tengzhou, he promoted learning and nurtured scholars, transforming its customs entirely; from then on Teng had candidates for the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Tengzhou he fostered schools and scholars and wholly changed local custom, so that Teng thereafter produced jinshi candidates.

sentences.zh: 通判海州，提點利州路刑獄。

translations.literal: He served as vice-prefect of Haizhou and as judicial intendant on the Lizhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was vice-prefect of Haizhou and judicial intendant on the Lizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 官罷，知泉州。

translations.literal: When he left office he was made prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving that post he was appointed prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書度支員外郎、廣南東路轉運使，擢秘書少監、知廣州，捕斬賊馮佐臣。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Outer Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and transport commissioner on the Guangnan East circuit, was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and prefect of Guangzhou, and captured and beheaded the bandit Feng Zuochen.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Outer Vice Director of Revenue and transport commissioner on the Guangnan East circuit, became Vice Director of the Secretariat and prefect of Guangzhou, and captured and executed the bandit Feng Zuochen.

sentences.zh: 入判大理寺，出知越州，復歸判尚書刑部，出知江寧府，歷右諫議大夫、給事中、知揚州，徙明州。

translations.literal: He entered to serve on the Court of Judicial Review, went out as prefect of Yuezhou, returned to serve again on the Ministry of Justice, went out as prefect of Jiangning prefecture, and served successively as Right Remonstrance Official, Drafting Official, and prefect of Yangzhou, then was transferred to Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sat on the Court of Judicial Review, served as prefect of Yuezhou, returned to the Ministry of Justice, went out as prefect of Jiangning, and held in turn the posts of Right Remonstrance Official, Drafting Official, and prefect of Yangzhou before transfer to Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以尚書工部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: He retired on office as Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the rank of Vice Director of Works.

sentences.zh: 祀明堂，遷刑部。

translations.literal: At the worship of the Bright Hall he was moved to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall sacrifice he was promoted within the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十有九，特贈吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-nine; he was specially posthumously made Vice Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-nine and was specially granted the posthumous title of Vice Director of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 簡性和易，喜賓客。

translations.literal: Jian's nature was genial and easy; he delighted in guests.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was mild and easygoing and loved to entertain guests.

sentences.zh: 即錢塘城北治園廬，自號「武林居士」。

translations.literal: North of Qiantang city he laid out a garden lodge and styled himself "Retired Gentleman of Wulin."
translations.idiomatic: North of Qiantang he built a garden retreat and called himself the Retired Gentleman of Wulin.

sentences.zh: 道引服餌，晚歲顏如丹。

translations.literal: He practiced Daoist breathing and medicinal regimens; in his later years his complexion was like cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Daoist breathing exercises and elixirs, and in his later years his face was as ruddy as cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 尤好醫術，人有疾，多自處方以療之，有集驗方數十，行於世。

translations.literal: He was especially fond of medicine; when people were ill he often prescribed for them himself, and had several dozen collected proven prescriptions circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled in medicine, often prescribing for the sick himself, and published several dozen tested formulas that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 一日，謂其子絜曰：「吾退居十五年，未嘗小不懌，今意倦，豈不逝歟？」

translations.literal: One day he said to his son Jie: "In my fifteen years since retirement I have never once been the least displeased; now I feel weary—is it not time to go?
translations.idiomatic: One day he told his son Jie, "In the fifteen years since I retired I have never once been out of sorts; now I feel tired—surely it is time to go?

sentences.zh: 就寢而絕。

translations.literal: He lay down to sleep and passed away.
translations.idiomatic: He lay down to sleep and died.

sentences.zh: 幼從學四明朱頔，長學文於沈天錫，既仕，均奉資之。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Zhu Wan of Siming; later he studied letters under Shen Tianxi; once in office he supported both with stipends.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he studied under Zhu Wan of Siming; later he studied literature under Shen Tianxi, and once in office he supported both men with stipends.

sentences.zh: 後二人亡，又訪其子孫，為主婚嫁。

translations.literal: After the two men died he sought out their descendants and arranged their marriages.
translations.idiomatic: After they died he sought out their descendants and arranged marriages for them.

sentences.zh: 平居宴語，惟以宣上德、救民患為意。

translations.literal: In ordinary conversation at table his sole thoughts were to proclaim the sovereign's virtue and relieve the people's woes.
translations.idiomatic: In everyday talk his only themes were to spread the emperor's virtue and ease the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 孫沔知杭州，榜其里門曰「德壽坊」。

translations.literal: Sun Mian when prefect of Hangzhou posted a placard on his lane gate calling it "Hall of Virtuous Longevity."
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Mian was prefect of Hangzhou he posted a placard on Jian's lane gate naming it the Hall of Virtuous Longevity.

sentences.zh: 然在廣州無廉稱，蓋為絜所累。

translations.literal: Yet in Guangzhou he had no reputation for integrity—probably because Jie compromised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had no reputation for integrity in Guangzhou, probably because his son Jie tarnished him.

sentences.zh: 絜，終尚書都官員外郎。

translations.literal: Jie ended as Outer Vice Director in the Ministry of State Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Jie ended his career as Outer Vice Director in the Ministry of State Revenue.

sentences.zh: 孫祖德

translations.literal: Sun Zude
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zude

sentences.zh: 孫祖德，字延仲，濰州北海人。

translations.literal: Sun Zude, styled Yanzhong, was a native of Beihai in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zude, courtesy name Yanzhong, was from Beihai in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 父航，監察御史、淮南轉運。

translations.literal: His father Hang was a investigating censor and transport commissioner on the Huainan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hang served as investigating censor and Huainan transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 祖德進士及第，調濠州推官、校勘館閣書籍。

translations.literal: Zude passed the jinshi and was appointed judicial assistant in Haozhou and collator of books in the palace library.
translations.idiomatic: Zude passed the jinshi and was made judicial assistant in Haozhou and a collator in the palace library.

sentences.zh: 時校勘官不為常職，滿歲而去。

translations.literal: At that time collators were not regular posts; they left after one year.
translations.idiomatic: Collators were not standing appointments then and left after a year.

sentences.zh: 改大理寺丞、知榆次縣，上書言刑法重輕。

translations.literal: He was changed to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Yuci County; he memorialized on the severity and leniency of penal law.
translations.idiomatic: He became an assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Yuci, and memorialized on the weight of punishments.

sentences.zh: 以尚書屯田員外郎通判西京留守司。

translations.literal: He was appointed Outer Assistant Director in the Ministry of Agriculture and vice prefect of the Western Capital garrison command.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Outer Assistant Director of Agriculture and vice prefect of the Western Capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 方冬苦寒，詔罷內外工作，而錢惟演督修天津橋，格詔不下。

translations.literal: In deep winter with severe cold, an edict halted inside and outside construction work, but Qian Weiyan supervised repair of the Tianjin Bridge and withheld the edict without implementing it.
translations.idiomatic: In the depth of winter an edict stopped all public works inside and out, yet Qian Weiyan pressed on with repairs to the Tianjin Bridge and held back the edict.

sentences.zh: 祖德曰：「詔書可稽留耶？」

translations.literal: Zude said: "Can an edict be held back?"
translations.idiomatic: Zude said, "Can an imperial edict be detained?"

sentences.zh: 卒白罷役。

translations.literal: In the end he reported it and the labor was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he reported the matter and the work was halted.

sentences.zh: 入為殿中侍御史，遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He entered as palace censor and was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as palace censor and was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 章獻太后春秋高，疾加劇，祖德請還政。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhangxian was advanced in years and her illness grew severe; Zude requested that she return the government.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian was old and gravely ill, Zude asked her to return rule to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 已而疾少間，祖德大恐。

translations.literal: Soon after her illness eased somewhat, and Zude was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Soon her illness lightened somewhat, and Zude was greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 及太后崩，諸嘗言還政者多進用，遂擢尚書兵部員外郎兼起居舍人、知諫院。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, of those who had spoken of returning the government many were promoted; he was thereupon raised to Outer Assistant Director in the Ministry of War with concurrent appointment as recorder and head of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager died, many who had urged the return of power were promoted, and Zude was raised to Outer Assistant Director of War with concurrent posts as recorder and head of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 言郭皇后不當廢，獲罪，以贖論。

translations.literal: He spoke saying Empress Guo should not have been deposed and was punished, commuted to a fine.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Empress Guo should not have been deposed, was punished, and the sentence was commuted to a fine.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷天章閣待制。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted to waiting gentleman of the Tianzhang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was made a waiting gentleman of the Tianzhang Hall.

sentences.zh: 時三司判官許申因宦官閻文應獻計，以藥化鐵成銅，可鑄錢，裨國用。

translations.literal: At that time the Three Departments judge Xu Shen, through the eunuch Yan Wenying, presented a plan to transform iron into copper by medicine so as to cast coin and benefit state revenues.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xu Shen, a judge of the Three Departments, through the eunuch Yan Wenying proposed using drugs to turn iron into copper for coinage to enrich the treasury.

sentences.zh: 祖德言：「偽銅，法所禁而官自為，是教民欺也。」

translations.literal: Zude said: "Counterfeit copper is forbidden by law, yet the government does it itself—is this not teaching the people to cheat?"
translations.idiomatic: Zude said, "Spurious copper is banned by law, yet the state would make it itself—is that not teaching the people to deceive?"

sentences.zh: 固爭之，出知兗徐蔡州、永興軍。

translations.literal: He argued firmly and was sent out as prefect of Yan, Xu, and Cai prefectures and of Yongxing army.
translations.idiomatic: He protested firmly and was sent out to govern Yan, Xu, and Cai and the Yongxing command.

sentences.zh: 徙鳳翔府，請置鄉兵。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Fengxiang prefecture and requested establishment of local militia.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Fengxiang, he petitioned to establish local militia.

sentences.zh: 改龍圖閣直學士、知梓州，累遷右諫議大夫、知河中府。

translations.literal: He was changed to academician in the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Zizhou, and was repeatedly promoted to Right Remonstrance Official and prefect of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He became an academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Zizhou, then rose to Right Remonstrance Official and prefect of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 歷陳許蔡潞鄆亳州、應天府，以疾得潁州，除吏部侍郎致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Chen, Xu, Cai, Lu, Yun, and Bozhou and of Yingtian prefecture; through illness he obtained Yingzhou; he was made Vice Director of Personnel and retired, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He governed in turn Chen, Xu, Cai, Lu, Yun, Bozhou, and Yingtian; through illness he secured Yingzhou, retired as Vice Director of Personnel, and died.

sentences.zh: 有《論事》七卷。

translations.literal: He had Discourses on Affairs in seven fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He left Discourses on Affairs in seven fascicles.

sentences.zh: 祖德少清約，及致仕，娶富人妻，以規有其財。

translations.literal: Zude was sparing and clean in his youth; after retirement he married a rich man's wife to scheme for her property.
translations.idiomatic: Zude had been frugal and upright in youth, but after retiring he married a rich man's wife to get her wealth.

sentences.zh: 已而妻悍，反資以財而出之。

translations.literal: Later his wife was fierce and instead paid him money to divorce her.
translations.idiomatic: The wife proved fierce and in the end paid him to leave her.

sentences.zh: 子珪，江東轉運使。

translations.literal: His son Gui was transport commissioner on the Jiangdong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui became Jiangdong transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 張若谷

translations.literal: Zhang Ruogu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ruogu

sentences.zh: 張若谷，字德繇，南劍沙縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ruogu, styled Deyou, was a native of Shaxian in Nanjian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ruogu, courtesy name Deyou, was from Shaxian in Nanjian.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，為巴州軍事推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and was appointed military judicial assistant in Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and was made military judicial assistant in Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 會蜀寇掠鄰郡，若谷攝州事，率眾為守禦備，賊乃引去。

translations.literal: When Shu bandits plundered neighboring prefectures, Ruogu acted in the prefect's stead, led the people in defense preparations, and the bandits then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu raiders looted neighboring prefectures, Ruogu acted as prefect, rallied the people in defense, and the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 調全州軍事推官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military judicial assistant in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military judicial assistant in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 入見，真宗識其名，顧曰：「是嘗在巴州禦賊者耶？」

translations.literal: On entering audience the emperor recognized his name and looked back saying: "Is this not the one who once defended against bandits in Bazhou?"
translations.idiomatic: At court the emperor recognized his name and said, "Is this not the man who once held off bandits in Bazhou?"

sentences.zh: 特改大理寺丞、知蒙陽縣。

translations.literal: He was specially changed to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Mengyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially made an assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Mengyang.

sentences.zh: 三司言：「廣寧監歲鑄緡錢四十萬，其主監宜擇人。」

translations.literal: The Three Departments reported: "The Guangning Mint casts four hundred thousand strings of cash yearly; the chief superintendent should be chosen with care."
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments reported, "The Guangning mint casts four hundred thousand strings of cash a year; its superintendent should be chosen carefully."

sentences.zh: 乃以命若谷。

translations.literal: He was then appointed to the post.
translations.idiomatic: Ruogu was appointed.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，所鑄贏三十萬緡。

translations.literal: In a little over a year the mint produced thirty thousand strings beyond the quota.
translations.idiomatic: In a little more than a year the mint turned out thirty thousand strings above quota.

sentences.zh: 擢知處州，歷江湖淮南益州路轉運、江淮制置發運使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Chuzhou and successively served as transport commissioner on the Jianghu, Huainan, and Yizhou circuits and as salt distribution commissioner for the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Chuzhou and served in turn as transport commissioner on the Jianghu, Huainan, and Yizhou circuits and as Jiang-Huai salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入為三司度支、鹽鐵副使，累遷右諫議大夫、知并州。

translations.literal: He entered as deputy vice-director of the Three Departments for Revenue and Salt Iron, and was repeatedly promoted to Right Remonstrance Official and prefect of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as deputy vice-director of Revenue and Salt Iron in the Three Departments and rose to Right Remonstrance Official and prefect of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，麟、府歲以繒錦市蕃部馬，前守輒罷之。

translations.literal: Previously Lin and Fu prefectures each year used silk and brocade to trade for tribal horses, and successive prefects had repeatedly halted the trade.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Lin and Fu each year traded silk and brocade for tribal horses, but successive prefects kept shutting the markets down.

sentences.zh: 若谷以謂：互市，所以利戎落而通邊情，且中國得戰馬；

translations.literal: Ruogu held that mutual markets benefit the frontier tribes and keep border sentiment open, while China also obtains war horses;
translations.idiomatic: Ruogu argued that border trade profits the frontier peoples, keeps border ties open, and brings war horses to the empire;

sentences.zh: 亟罷之，則猜阻不安。

translations.literal: to halt them repeatedly would breed suspicion and unrest.
translations.idiomatic: to abolish it again and again would only breed suspicion and unrest.

sentences.zh: 奏復市如故，而馬入歲增。

translations.literal: He memorialized to restore trade as before, and horse imports increased year by year.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to restore the markets as before, and horse imports rose each year.

sentences.zh: 提舉諸司庫務，權判大理寺，進樞密直學士，歷知澶州、成德軍、揚州、江寧府，入知審官院，糾察在京刑獄，知通進銀臺司、應天府。

translations.literal: He supervised the various treasury offices, served as acting president of the Court of Judicial Review, was promoted to Academician in the Council of State, successively served as prefect of Danzhou, the Chengde army command, Yangzhou, and Jiangning prefecture, entered to head the Bureau of Appointments, inspected capital criminal cases, and directed the Office for Transmission of Memorials and Yingtian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw treasury offices, acted as president of the Court of Judicial Review, rose to Academician in the Council of State, governed Danzhou, Chengde, Yangzhou, and Jiangning, headed the Bureau of Appointments, inspected capital criminal cases, and directed the memorials office and Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 改龍圖閣學士，徙杭州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Academician in the Dragon Diagram Hall and transferred to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became an academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and was transferred to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會歲饑，斥餘廩為糜粥賑救之。

translations.literal: When famine struck that year he released surplus granary stores to make gruel for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck he opened surplus granaries and distributed porridge for relief.

sentences.zh: 權判吏部流內銓、知洪州，累官至尚書左丞致仕。

translations.literal: He acted as director of the Bureau of Personnel Rosters in the Ministry of Personnel and as prefect of Hongzhou, and rose in rank to retire as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He acted as head of the roster bureau and as prefect of Hongzhou, and eventually retired as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 若谷素為宰相張士遜引拔，然所至亦自有循良跡，不激訐取名云。

translations.literal: Ruogu had long been advanced by Chief Minister Zhang Shisun, yet wherever he served he also left traces of honest and gentle rule, not seeking a reputation by harsh denunciation.
translations.idiomatic: Ruogu had been promoted by Chief Minister Zhang Shisun, yet in each post he also left a record of honest administration without courting fame through harsh attacks.

sentences.zh: 石揚休

translations.literal: Shi Yangxiu
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yangxiu

sentences.zh: 石揚休，字昌言，其先江都人。

translations.literal: Shi Yangxiu, styled Changyan, was originally from Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yangxiu, courtesy name Changyan, traced his origins to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 唐兵部郎中仲覽之後，後徙京兆。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Zhonglan, Vice Director in the Ministry of War in Tang; later the family moved to Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His line descended from Tang Vice Director of War Zhonglan and later moved to Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 七代祖藏用，右羽林大將軍，明於曆數，嘗召家人謂曰：「天下將有變，而蜀為最安處。」

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Zangyong was a general of the Right Feathered Forest and skilled in calendrical reckoning; he once summoned his family and said: "The realm will soon be in turmoil, and Shu will be the safest place."
translations.idiomatic: His seventh-generation ancestor Zangyong, a general of the Right Feathered Forest, was skilled in calendrical science; he once told his family, "The realm will soon be in turmoil, and Shu will be the safest refuge."

sentences.zh: 乃去依其親眉州刺史李滈，遂為眉州人。

translations.literal: He then left to join his kinsman Li Hao, military governor of Meizhou, and thus became a man of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went to join his kinsman Li Hao, military governor of Meizhou, and the family became Meizhou people.

sentences.zh: 揚休少孤力學，進士高第，為同州觀察推官，遷著作佐郎、知中牟縣。

translations.literal: Yangxiu was orphaned young and studied hard; he passed the jinshi in the top grade and was appointed judicial assistant to the Tongzhou surveillance commissioner, then promoted to Assistant Compiler and magistrate of Zhongmou County.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Yangxiu studied hard, took the jinshi in the highest class, served as judicial assistant in Tongzhou, and was promoted to assistant compiler and magistrate of Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 縣當國西門，衣冠往來之衝也，地瘠民貧，賦役煩重，富人隸太常為樂工，僥幸免役者凡六十餘家。

translations.literal: The county lay at the western gate of the capital, on the thoroughfare of officials and gentry coming and going; the land was poor and the people impoverished, taxes and corvée heavy, and over sixty wealthy households had enrolled as musicians under the Imperial Sacrifices to evade labor.
translations.idiomatic: The county stood at the empire's western gate on the road of officials and gentry; the land was poor, taxes heavy, and more than sixty wealthy households had registered as Imperial Sacrifice musicians to escape corvée.

sentences.zh: 揚休請悉罷之。

translations.literal: Yangxiu requested that all of them be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxiu petitioned to abolish every such exemption.

sentences.zh: 改秘書丞，為秘閣校理、開封府推官，累遷尚書祠部員外郎，歷三司度支、鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: He was changed to Secretary Director, served as collator in the palace library and judicial officer of Kaifeng prefecture, and was repeatedly promoted to Outer Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites and served as judge in the Three Departments for Revenue and Salt Iron.
translations.idiomatic: He became a secretary director, collator in the palace library, and Kaifeng judicial officer, then rose to Outer Vice Director of Rites and judge in Revenue and Salt Iron.

sentences.zh: 坐前在開封嘗失盜，出知宿州。

translations.literal: He was punished because while previously in Kaifeng a theft had occurred on his watch, and was sent out as prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because a theft had occurred in Kaifeng while he served there, he was sent out as prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，召入為度支判官，修起居注。

translations.literal: Soon after he was recalled as judge in the Revenue Department and compiler of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as revenue judge and compiler of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 初，記注官與講讀諸儒，皆得侍坐邇英閣。

translations.literal: At first recorders and the various lecturers in the lecture hall all had seats beside the emperor in the Yingying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At first recorders and lecture-hall scholars all sat beside the emperor in the Yingying Hall.

sentences.zh: 揚休奏：「史官記言動，當立以侍。」

translations.literal: Yangxiu memorialized: "Historians who record words and deeds should stand in attendance."
translations.idiomatic: Yangxiu memorialized, "Historians who record words and deeds should stand to attend."

sentences.zh: 從其言。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 判鹽鐵勾院，以刑部員外郎知制誥、同判太常寺。

translations.literal: He served as judge of the Salt Iron Audit Office, and as Outer Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments with concurrent appointment as drafting official and associate director of the Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He judged the Salt Iron Audit Office and served as Outer Vice Director of Punishments with concurrent posts as drafting official and associate director of the Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 初，內出香祠溫成廟，帝誤書名稱臣，揚休言：「此奉宗廟禮，有司承誤不以聞。」

translations.literal: At first incense was issued from within the palace for the Wen Cheng temple; the emperor mistakenly wrote his title as "your minister"; Yangxiu said: "This is a rite for the ancestral temple—the responsible office should report the error and not keep silent."
translations.idiomatic: When incense was issued for the Wen Cheng temple, the emperor mistakenly wrote "your minister"; Yangxiu said, "This is an ancestral rite—the responsible office should report the error rather than keep silent."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 兼勾當三班院，為宗正寺修玉牒官。

translations.literal: He concurrently oversaw the Third-Rank Bureau and served as compiler of the imperial genealogy in the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He also oversaw the Third-Rank Bureau and compiled the imperial genealogy in the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 遷工部郎中，未及謝，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works; before he could offer thanks he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of Works but died before he could offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 揚休喜閑放，平居養猿鶴，玩圖書，吟詠自適，與家人言，未嘗及朝廷事。

translations.literal: Yangxiu loved leisure and freedom; in ordinary life he kept apes and cranes, enjoyed books and pictures, and composed poetry for his own pleasure; speaking with his family he never touched court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxiu loved a leisurely life, kept apes and cranes, read and wrote poetry for pleasure, and never discussed court affairs with his family.

sentences.zh: 及卒，發楮中所得上封事十餘章，其大略：請增諫官以廣言路，置五經博士使學者專其業，出御史按察諸道以防壅蔽，復齒胄之禮以強宗室，擇守令，重農桑，禁奢侈，皆有補於時者。

translations.literal: When he died, more than a dozen sealed memorials to the throne were found among his papers, broadly urging: increase remonstrance officials to broaden counsel, appoint Five Classics doctors so scholars may specialize, send out investigating censors on the circuits to prevent obstruction, restore the ceremony of heirs attending school to strengthen the imperial clan, choose prefects and magistrates, emphasize agriculture and sericulture, and forbid luxury—all measures that would have benefited the age.
translations.idiomatic: After his death a dozen sealed memorials were found, broadly urging more remonstrance officials, Five Classics doctors, circuit censors, restored heir-school rites, careful choice of prefects and magistrates, emphasis on farming, and bans on luxury—all useful to the times.

sentences.zh: 然揚休為人慎默，世未嘗以能言待之也。

translations.literal: Yet Yangxiu was cautious and reticent by nature; the world had never regarded him as one who could speak out.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was cautious and reticent, and the world had never counted him among those who spoke boldly.

sentences.zh: 至於誥命，尤非所長。

translations.literal: As for edicts and appointments, that was especially not his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting edicts was especially not his strength.

sentences.zh: 平生好殖財。

translations.literal: Throughout his life he loved to accumulate wealth.
translations.idiomatic: All his life he loved to amass wealth.

sentences.zh: 因使契丹，道感寒毒，得風痹，謁告歸鄉，別墳墓。

translations.literal: On a mission to the Khitan he contracted cold poison on the road, developed wind paralysis, requested leave to return home, and visited the family graves.
translations.idiomatic: On an embassy to the Khitan he caught a chill on the road, developed wind paralysis, asked leave to return home, and visited the family graves.

sentences.zh: 揚休初在鄉時，衣食不足，徙步去家十八年。

translations.literal: When Yangxiu was first in his home district food and clothing were insufficient; he walked away from home for eighteen years.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth at home he had lacked food and clothing and had been away on foot for eighteen years.

sentences.zh: 後以從官還鄉里，疇昔同貧窶之人尚在，皆曰：「昌言來，必賙我矣。」

translations.literal: Later, returning home as a court official, those who had once shared his poverty were still there and all said: "Changyan has come—he is sure to give us relief."
translations.idiomatic: When he later returned as a court official, his former poor neighbors all said, "Changyan has come—he is sure to give us something."

sentences.zh: 揚休卒不揮一金，反遍受里中富人金以去。

translations.literal: Yangxiu in the end did not give out a single cash; on the contrary he took money from wealthy men throughout the district and left.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he gave not a single coin but took money from wealthy neighbors all around and left.

sentences.zh: 祖士衡

translations.literal: Zu Shiheng
translations.idiomatic: Zu Shiheng

sentences.zh: 祖士衡，字平叔，蔡州上蔡人。

translations.literal: Zu Shiheng, styled Pingshu, was a native of Shangcai in Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Shiheng, courtesy name Pingshu, was from Shangcai in Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，博學有文，為李宗諤所知，妻以兄子。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was broadly learned and literary; Li Zonge took notice of him and married him to his elder brother's son's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was learned and literary; Li Zonge noticed him and married him to his brother's son's daughter.

sentences.zh: 楊億謂劉筠曰：「祖士衡辭學日新，後生可畏也。」

translations.literal: Yang Yi said to Liu Yun: "Zu Shiheng's literary learning renews itself day by day—the younger generation is to be feared."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi told Liu Yun, "Zu Shiheng's literary learning improves daily—the young man is formidable."

sentences.zh: 舉進士甲科，授大理評事、通判蘄州，再遷殿中丞、直集賢院，改右正言、戶部判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the top grade, was appointed reviewing officer in the Court of Judicial Review and vice-prefect of Qizhou, and was again promoted to Director in the Palace and collator in the Hall of Assembled Treasures, then changed to Right Rectifier and judge in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in the highest class, became a judicial reviewer and vice-prefect of Qizhou, then rose to palace director and collator in the Hall of Assembled Treasures, then Right Rectifier and revenue judge.

sentences.zh: 未幾，提舉在京諸司庫務，遷起居舍人、注釋御集檢閱官，遂知制誥，為史館修撰，糾察在京刑獄，同知通進銀臺司。

translations.literal: Before long he supervised the capital treasury offices, was promoted to Recorder and annotator and collator of the imperial collected writings, then drafting official, compiler in the History Office, inspector of capital criminal cases, and associate director of the Office for Transmission of Memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he supervised the capital treasuries, became recorder and collator of imperial writings, then drafting official, history compiler, capital criminal inspector, and associate director of the memorials office.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，以附丁謂，落職知吉州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tiansheng era, because he had attached himself to Ding Wei, he was demoted to prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tiansheng, for having sided with Ding Wei, he was demoted to prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 言者又以在郡不修飭，復降監江州稅。

translations.literal: Critics also charged that in the prefecture he did not maintain proper conduct, and he was again demoted to supervisor of the Jiangzhou tax office.
translations.idiomatic: Critics also said he had been lax in office, and he was demoted again to supervisor of the Jiangzhou tax office.

sentences.zh: 士衡兒時過外家，有僧善相，見之，語人曰：「是兒神骨秀異，他日有名於時，若年過四十，當位極人臣。」

translations.literal: In childhood when passing his maternal family's home, a monk skilled in physiognomy saw him and told others: "This boy has an extraordinary spirit and bones; he will be famous in his time; if he passes forty he will reach the highest ministerial rank."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy visiting his mother's family, a physiognomist said of him, "This child has extraordinary spirit; he will be famous; if he lives past forty he will reach the highest rank."

sentences.zh: 年三十九，卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office at thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 李垂，字舜工，聊城人。

translations.literal: Li Chui, styled Shungong, was a native of Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chui, courtesy name Shungong, was from Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，登進士第，上《兵製》、《將制書》。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era he passed the jinshi and submitted Military Regulations and Generalship.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianping era he passed the jinshi and submitted treatises on military organization and command.

sentences.zh: 自湖州錄事參軍召為崇文校勘，累遷著作郎、館閣校理。

translations.literal: From recorder in Huzhou he was summoned as collator in the Chongwen Institute and was repeatedly promoted to Compiler and collator in the palace library.
translations.idiomatic: From Huzhou recorder he was summoned as Chongwen collator and rose to compiler and palace collator.

sentences.zh: 上《導河形勝書》三卷，欲復九河故道，時論重之。

translations.literal: He submitted Guiding the River and Strategic Terrain in three fascicles, wishing to restore the old courses of the Nine Rivers; opinion at the time valued it highly.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted Guiding the River and Strategic Terrain in three fascicles, proposing to restore the Nine Rivers; contemporaries greatly valued it.

sentences.zh: 又累修起居注。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly revised the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly served as compiler of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 丁謂執政，垂未嘗往謁。

translations.literal: When Ding Wei held power, Chui never went to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Wei held power, Chui never called on him.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，垂曰：「謂為宰相，不以公道副天下望，而恃權怙勢。

translations.literal: When someone asked why, Chui said: "Wei serves as chief minister yet does not meet the world's hopes with public fairness, but relies on power and leans on influence.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "Wei is chief minister yet does not meet the world's hopes with fairness, but relies on power and patronage.

sentences.zh: 觀其所為，必遊朱崖，吾不欲在其黨中。」

translations.literal: Watching what he does, he is sure to end at Zhuya; I do not wish to be in his faction."
translations.idiomatic: Watch what he does—he is sure to end in exile on Hainan; I will not join his faction."

sentences.zh: 謂聞而惡之，罷知亳州，遷潁、晉、絳三州。

translations.literal: When Wei heard of it he hated him and removed him to prefect of Bozhou, then transferred him through Ying, Jin, and Jiang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Wei heard and hated him, demoted him to Bozhou, then moved him through Ying, Jin, and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 明道中，還朝，閤門祗候李康伯謂曰：「舜工文學議論稱於天下，諸公欲用為知制誥，但宰相以舜工未嘗相識，盍一往見之。」

translations.literal: In the Mingdao era he returned to court; Ceremonial Attendant Li Kangbo said to him: "Shungong's literary learning and discourse are famed throughout the realm; the gentlemen wish to use you as drafting official, but the chief minister says he does not know Shungong—why not go once to see him?"
translations.idiomatic: In Mingdao he returned to court; Li Kangbo said, "Your learning and discourse are famed; the gentlemen want you as drafting official, but the chief minister says he does not know you—why not visit him once?"

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「我若昔謁丁崖州，則乾興初已為翰林學士矣。

translations.literal: Chui said: "Had I once called on Ding of Yazhou, I would already have been a Hanlin academician in the Qianxing era.
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "Had I once called on Ding in exile, I would already have been Hanlin academician in Qianxing.

sentences.zh: 今已老大，見大臣不公，常欲面折之，焉能趨炎附熱，看人眉睫，以冀推輓乎？

translations.literal: Now I am old; when I see a great minister acting unfairly I often want to rebuke him to his face—how could I run after power and watch another's brow to seek promotion?
translations.idiomatic: Now I am old; when I see a minister act unfairly I want to rebuke him to his face—how could I chase power and watch another's brow for promotion?

sentences.zh: 道之不行，命也！」

translations.literal: If the Way does not prevail, that is fate!"
translations.idiomatic: If the Way does not prevail, that is fate!"

sentences.zh: 執政知之，出知均州。

translations.literal: The council learned of it and sent him out as prefect of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The council heard and sent him out as prefect of Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 五子，仲昌最知名，銳於進取，嘗獻計修六塔河無功，自殿中丞責英州文學參軍。

translations.literal: He had five sons; Zhongchang was most famous, keen to advance, once submitted a plan to repair the Six Pagoda River without success, and was demoted from Director in the Palace to literary adjutant in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Of five sons Zhongchang was best known, eager to advance; his plan to repair the Six Pagoda River failed, and he was demoted from palace director to literary adjutant in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 張洞，字仲通，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Zhang Dong, styled Zhongtong, was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dong, courtesy name Zhongtong, was from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父惟簡，太常少卿。

translations.literal: His father Weijian was Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His father Weijian was Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 洞為人長大，眉目如畫，自幼開悟，卓犖不群。

translations.literal: Dong was tall in stature, his eyebrows and eyes like a painting; from childhood he was quick to understand and stood apart from the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Dong was tall, with brows and eyes like a painting; from boyhood he was quick-witted and stood apart.

sentences.zh: 惟簡異之，抱以訪里之卜者。

translations.literal: Weijian marveled at him and carried him to visit a diviner in the lane.
translations.idiomatic: Weijian marveled at him and took him to a neighborhood diviner.

sentences.zh: 曰：「郎君生甚奇，必在策名，後當以文學政事顯。」

translations.literal: The man said: "This young master's birth is very strange; he is sure to win a degree; later he will be illustrious in letters and administration."
translations.idiomatic: The man said, "This boy's birth is extraordinary; he will win a degree and later shine in letters and administration."

sentences.zh: 既誦書，日數千言，為文甚敏。

translations.literal: Once he began reading books he recited several thousand characters a day and wrote with great speed.
translations.idiomatic: Once he read books he recited thousands of characters a day and wrote with great speed.

sentences.zh: 未冠，曄然有聲，遇事慷慨，自許以有為。

translations.literal: Before cap and sash he was already renowned; encountering affairs he was bold and generous, trusting himself to accomplish something.
translations.idiomatic: Before coming of age he was already famed; in affairs he was bold and promised himself achievement.

sentences.zh: 時，趙元昊叛擾邊。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Yuanhao rebelled and harassed the border.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao Yuanhao rebelled and raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 關、隴蕭然，困於飛輓，且屢喪師。

translations.literal: Guan and Long were desolate; transport by draft animals was strained, and the army repeatedly suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Long lay waste; supply lines were strained and the army suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 仁宗太息，思聞中外之謀。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong sighed deeply and wished to hear counsel from within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong sighed and wished to hear counsel from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 洞以布衣求上方略，召試舍人院，擢試將作監主簿。

translations.literal: Dong as a commoner sought to present strategy to the throne; he was summoned to test in the Academy and was promoted to probationary director in the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Dong as a commoner offered strategy to the throne, was tested in the Academy, and was made probationary director of works.

sentences.zh: 尋舉進士中第，調漣水軍判官，遭親喪去，再調潁州推官。

translations.literal: Soon he passed the jinshi and was appointed judicial officer of the Lianshui army; he left on mourning for a parent, then was reassigned as judicial officer in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he passed the jinshi, served as judicial officer in Lianshui, left on mourning, then was reassigned to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 民劉甲者，強弟柳使鞭其婦，既而投杖，夫婦相持而泣。

translations.literal: A man named Liu Jia forced his younger brother Liu Liu to whip Liu's wife; afterward he threw down the stick and husband and wife held each other weeping.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Liu Jia forced his brother Liu Liu to whip Jia's wife; then he threw down the stick and the couple clung to each other weeping.

sentences.zh: 甲怒，逼柳使再鞭之。

translations.literal: Jia grew angry and forced Liu to whip her again.
translations.idiomatic: Jia grew angry and forced Liu to whip her again.

sentences.zh: 婦以無罪死。

translations.literal: The wife died though guilty of no crime.
translations.idiomatic: The wife died though she was innocent.

sentences.zh: 吏當夫極法，知州歐陽修欲從之。

translations.literal: The clerk would punish the husband with the extreme penalty; Prefect Ouyang Xiu wished to agree.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk would punish the husband with death; Prefect Ouyang Xiu wished to agree.

sentences.zh: 洞曰：「律以教令者為首，夫為從，且非其意，不當死。」

translations.literal: Dong said: "The law makes the one who issues the command the principal and the husband the accessory; moreover it was not his intent—he should not die."
translations.idiomatic: Dong said, "The law makes the one who commands the beating the principal and the husband the accessory; it was not his intent—he should not die."

sentences.zh: 眾不聽，洞即稱疾不出，不得已讞於朝，果如洞言，修甚重之。

translations.literal: The assembly would not listen; Dong then claimed illness and would not appear; forced to refer the case to court, the result was as Dong said, and Xiu greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly would not listen; Dong claimed illness and stayed away; the case went to court and ended as Dong said, and Xiu greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 晏殊知永興軍，奏管勾機宜文字。

translations.literal: Yan Shu when military governor of Yongxing memorialized him as staff officer for military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Shu governed Yongxing he memorialized Dong as staff officer for military affairs.

sentences.zh: 殊儒臣，喜客，遊其門者皆名士，尤深敬洞。

translations.literal: Shu was a Confucian minister who loved guests; those who visited his gate were all famous men, and he especially respected Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was a Confucian who loved guests; his visitors were all famous men, and he especially respected Dong.

sentences.zh: 改大理丞、知鞏縣。

translations.literal: Dong was changed to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Gong County.
translations.idiomatic: Dong became an assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Gong County.

sentences.zh: 會殊留守西京，復奏知司錄。

translations.literal: When Shu remained at the Western Capital, he again memorialized him as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu remained at the Western Capital he again memorialized him as recorder.

sentences.zh: 殊晚節驟用刑，幕府無敢言。

translations.literal: In his late years Shu suddenly used punishments heavily, and no one in the staff dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: In his late years Shu suddenly used punishments heavily and no one in his staff dared speak.

sentences.zh: 洞平居與殊賦詩飲酒，傾倒無不至，當事有官責，持議甚堅，殊為沮止，洞亦自以不負其知。

translations.literal: Dong in ordinary times composed poetry and drank wine with Shu with complete abandon; when there was official business with responsibility he held to his view very firmly, and Shu was checked and stopped—Dong also felt he had not betrayed Shu's trust in him.
translations.idiomatic: In private Dong drank and wrote poetry with Shu without reserve; in official business he held firm, checked Shu, and felt he had not betrayed his trust.

sentences.zh: 初，皇后郭氏忤旨得罪廢沒，後仁宗悔之，詔追復其號，二十餘年矣。

translations.literal: At first Empress Guo had offended the emperor's intent and was deposed and died; later Renzong regretted it and issued an edict restoring her title, more than twenty years having passed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Guo had once offended the emperor and was deposed and died; later Renzong regretted it and restored her title after more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 至是，有司請祔於廟。

translations.literal: Now the responsible offices requested that she be enshrined in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Now the responsible offices asked to enshrine her in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 知制誥劉敞以謂：「《春秋》書『禘於太廟，用致夫人』。

translations.literal: Drafting Official Liu Chang held that "the Bright Hall sacrifice with the wife presented" in the Spring and Autumn means presentation.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Official Liu Chang cited the Spring and Autumn: "Sacrifice at the Bright Hall with the wife presented.

sentences.zh: 致者，不宜致也。

translations.literal: To present is what should not be presented."
translations.idiomatic: To present means what ought not to be presented.

sentences.zh: 且古者不二嫡，當許其號，不許其禮。」

translations.literal: Moreover in antiquity there was no second primary wife; her title may be granted but not the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity there was no second primary wife; grant the title but not the rite."

sentences.zh: 洞奏：「后嘗母天下，無大過惡，中外所知。

translations.literal: Dong memorialized: "The empress once mothered the realm and had no great fault known within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Dong memorialized, "The empress once mothered the realm without great fault known to all.

sentences.zh: 陛下既察其偶失恭順，洗之於既沒，猶曰不許其禮，於義無當。

translations.literal: The emperor has already seen her occasional lapse in respectful obedience and washed it away after her death—yet to say her rite may not be granted is without justification in principle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has already forgiven her lapse after death—yet to deny her rite is unjust.

sentences.zh: 且廢后立后，何嫌於嫡？

translations.literal: Moreover when a deposed empress is replaced by a new empress, what scruple is there about primary status?
translations.idiomatic: When one empress replaces another, what scruple remains about primary status?

sentences.zh: 此當時大臣護已然之失，乖正名之典，而敞復引《春秋》『用致夫人』。

translations.literal: This was the great ministers of that time protecting an error already made and departing from the canon of correct naming; yet Chang again cites the Spring and Autumn phrase "with the wife presented.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers then protected an established error; Chang again cites the phrase "with the wife presented."

sentences.zh: 按《左氏》哀姜之惡所不忍道，而二《傳》有非嫡之辭，敞議非是。

translations.literal: According to the Zuo Commentary the wickedness of Ai Jiang is unspeakable, and the two commentaries contain language of non-primary status—Chang's argument is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary shows Ai Jiang's wickedness; the two commentaries speak of non-primary status—Chang is wrong.

sentences.zh: 若從變禮，尚當別立廟。」

translations.literal: If one follows altered rites, a separate temple should still be established."
translations.idiomatic: Even under altered rites a separate temple should be set up."

sentences.zh: 不行。

translations.literal: The proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 轉太常博士，判登聞鼓院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Doctor in the Imperial Sacrifices and president of the Drum Court for Appeals.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Doctor of the Imperial Sacrifices and president of the Drum Court for Appeals.

sentences.zh: 仁宗方向儒術，洞在館閣久，數有建明，仁宗以為知《經》，會覆考進士崇政殿，因賜飛白「善經」字寵之。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong was turning toward Confucian learning; Dong had long served in the palace academies and repeatedly put forward clear proposals; Renzong considered him knowledgeable in the Classics; when he was re-examining jinshi at Chongzheng Hall, he bestowed the feibai characters "Good at the Classics" to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong was turning toward Confucian learning, and Dong, who had long served in the palace academies and often offered sound proposals, was thought by the emperor to know the Classics well; during a jinshi re-examination at Chongzheng Hall, Renzong honored him with feibai calligraphy reading "Good at the Classics."

sentences.zh: 洞獻詩謝，復賜詔獎諭。

translations.literal: Dong submitted a poem of thanks, and an edict of commendation was bestowed again.
translations.idiomatic: Dong submitted a poem of thanks, and the emperor again issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 出知棣州，轉尚書祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Dizhou and was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites' Sacrifices Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Dizhou and promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites' Sacrifices Bureau.

sentences.zh: 河北地當六塔之衝者，歲決溢病民田。

translations.literal: In Hebei, land at the choke point of the Six Towers overflowed every year and harmed the people's fields.
translations.idiomatic: In Hebei, land in the flood path of the Six Towers project overflowed yearly and ruined the people's fields.

sentences.zh: 水退，強者遂冒占，弱者耕居無所。

translations.literal: When the water receded, the strong seized and occupied land, while the weak had nowhere to farm or live.
translations.idiomatic: After the floods receded, the strong seized the land while the weak had nowhere to farm or dwell.

sentences.zh: 洞奏一切官為標給，蠲其租以綏新集。

translations.literal: Dong memorialized that the government should mark and allocate all of it and remit rents to pacify newly settled people.
translations.idiomatic: Dong memorialized that the state should mark and register all such land, remit its rents, and thereby settle the newly displaced.

sentences.zh: 河北東路民富蠶桑，契丹謂之「綾絹州」，朝廷以為內地不慮。

translations.literal: The people of Eastern Hebei Circuit were rich in mulberry and sericulture; the Khitan called it the "Silk Gauze Circuit," and the court regarded it as interior land and felt no concern.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Hebei was rich in mulberry and sericulture, and the Khitan called it the "Silk Gauze Circuit"; the court treated it as interior territory and saw little cause for worry.

sentences.zh: 洞奏：「今滄、景，契丹可入之道，兵守多缺，契丹時以販鹽為名，舟往來境上，此不可不察。

translations.literal: Dong memorialized: "Cangzhou and Jingzhou are now routes by which the Khitan can enter; military garrisons are largely short; the Khitan sometimes under the pretext of selling salt send boats back and forth along the border—this must not go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: Dong memorialized, "Cangzhou and Jingzhou are now avenues of Khitan entry, garrisons are often understrength, and the Khitan sometimes move boats along the border under the guise of trading salt—this cannot be overlooked.

sentences.zh: 願度形勢，置帥、增屯戍以控扼之。」

translations.literal: I wish to assess the terrain, appoint commanders, and increase garrisons to control and block them."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we survey the terrain, appoint commanders, and add garrisons to hold the line."

sentences.zh: 時天下久安，薦紳崇尚虛名，以寬厚沉默為德，於事無所補，洞以謂非朝廷福。

translations.literal: At the time the realm had long been at peace; officials prized empty reputation and took generosity and silence as virtue, helping nothing in affairs—Dong held that this was no blessing to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The empire had long been at peace, and officials prized empty reputation, treating leniency and silence as virtue while contributing nothing to affairs; Dong held that this boded ill for the court.

sentences.zh: 又謂：「諫官持諫以震人主，不數年至顯仕，此何為者？

translations.literal: He also said: "Remonstrance officials wield remonstrance to startle the sovereign, and within a few years reach prominent office—what is the point of this?
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Remonstrance officials brandish remonstrance to startle the throne, then within a few years rise to high office—what is that for?

sentences.zh: 當重其任而緩其遷，使端良之士不亟易，而浮躁者絕意。」

translations.literal: Their duties should be weighted heavily and their promotions slowed, so upright men are not quickly changed and the restless give up the idea."
translations.idiomatic: We should weight their responsibilities and slow their promotions, so upright men are not quickly replaced and the restless abandon the pursuit."

sentences.zh: 致書歐陽修極論之。

translations.literal: He wrote to Ouyang Xiu arguing this at length.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Ouyang Xiu and argued the point at length.

sentences.zh: 召權開封府推官。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as acting investigating officer of Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as acting investigating officer of Kaifeng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，轉度支員外郎。

translations.literal: When Yingzong acceded, he was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue's Finance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong came to the throne, he was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue's Finance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 英宗哀疚，或經旬不御正殿，洞上言：「陛下春秋鼎盛，初嗣大統，豈宜久屈剛健，自比沖幼之主。

translations.literal: Yingzong was in mourning and sometimes went ten days without holding court in the main hall; Dong submitted: "Your Majesty is in the prime of life and has newly inherited the great succession—how can you long suppress your vigor and compare yourself to a young child sovereign?
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong was in mourning and sometimes went ten days without holding court in the main hall; Dong submitted, "Your Majesty is in the prime of life and has just inherited the throne—how can you long restrain your vigor and comport yourself like a child emperor?

sentences.zh: 當躬萬機，攬群材，以稱先帝付畀之意，厭元元之望。」

translations.literal: You should personally attend to the myriad affairs and gather talent, to answer the late emperor's trust and satisfy the people's hopes."
translations.idiomatic: You should personally handle the myriad affairs of state and gather able men, to fulfill the late emperor's charge and meet the people's expectations."

sentences.zh: 大臣亦以為言，遂聽政。

translations.literal: The great ministers also spoke thus, and the emperor then held court.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers spoke likewise, and the emperor thereupon resumed court.

sentences.zh: 命考試開封進士，既罷，進賦，題曰《孝慈則忠》，時方議濮安懿王稱皇事，英宗曰：「張洞意諷朕。」

translations.literal: He was ordered to examine Kaifeng jinshi; when the examination ended he submitted a rhapsody titled "Filial Piety and Kindness Then Loyalty"; at the time they were debating whether to call Prince An of Pu "Emperor"; Yingzong said: "Zhang Dong's meaning satirizes me.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to examine Kaifeng jinshi candidates, he submitted after the test a rhapsody titled "Filial Piety and Kindness Then Loyalty"; as the court was debating whether Prince An of Pu should be styled emperor, Yingzong said, "Zhang Dong means to satirize me.

sentences.zh: 宰相韓琦進曰：「言之者無罪，聞之者足以戒。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Han Qi stepped forward and said: "He who speaks is without guilt; he who hears may take warning."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Han Qi stepped forward and said, "The speaker is not guilty; the listener may take warning."

sentences.zh: 英宗意解。

translations.literal: Yingzong's mind was eased.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong's resentment eased.

sentences.zh: 詔訊祁國公宗說獄，宗說恃近屬，貴驕不道，獄具，英宗以為辱國，不欲暴其惡。

translations.literal: An edict ordered inquiry into the case of Duke of Qi Guo Zong Shuo; Zong Shuo relied on close kinship, was proud and lawless; when the case was complete Yingzong thought it shamed the state and did not wish to expose his wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: By edict the court investigated Duke of Qi Guo Zong Shuo; relying on his close kinship, he was arrogant and lawless; when the case was complete Yingzong felt it would shame the state and did not wish to expose his crimes.

sentences.zh: 洞曰：「宗說罪在不宥。

translations.literal: Dong said: "Zong Shuo's crime admits no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Dong said, "Zong Shuo's crime admits no pardon.

sentences.zh: 雖然，陛下將懲惡而難暴之，獨以其坑不辜數人，置諸法可矣。」

translations.literal: Still, Your Majesty wishes to punish evil yet finds it hard to expose him—merely punish him for burying alive several innocent people according to law will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Yet if Your Majesty wishes to punish wickedness without public exposure, you need only punish him for burying several innocent people alive under the law."

sentences.zh: 英宗喜曰：「卿知大體。」

translations.literal: Yingzong said with pleasure: "You know the larger principle."
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong said with pleasure, "You understand the larger principle."

sentences.zh: 洞因言：「唐宗室多賢宰相名士，蓋其知學問使然。

translations.literal: Dong then said: "In Tang many members of the imperial clan became worthy chief ministers and famous scholars—all because they studied learning.
translations.idiomatic: Dong then said, "In Tang many imperial clansmen became worthy chief ministers and famous scholars because they were trained in learning.

sentences.zh: 國家本支蕃衍，無親疏一切厚廩之，不使知辛苦。

translations.literal: Our state's collateral branches proliferate; without distinction of close or distant, all are lavishly supported and never know hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Our collateral branches have multiplied, and without regard to closeness or distance all are richly maintained and never know hardship.

sentences.zh: 婢妾聲伎，無多寡之限，至滅禮義，極嗜欲。

translations.literal: Concubines and entertainers have no limit on number, to the point of destroying ritual propriety and indulging desires to the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Concubines and entertainers are kept without limit, until ritual propriety is destroyed and desires are indulged to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 貸之則亂公共之法，刑之則傷骨肉之愛。

translations.literal: If you lend to them you disorder public law; if you punish them you wound familial love.
translations.idiomatic: To lend to them is to disorder public law; to punish them is to wound familial affection.

sentences.zh: 宜因秩品立制度，更選老成教授之。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to establish institutions by rank and grade and additionally select experienced men to instruct them."
translations.idiomatic: Institutions should be set by rank and grade, and seasoned men should be chosen to instruct them."

sentences.zh: 宗室緣是怨洞，痛詆訾言，上亦起藩邸，賴察之，不罪也。

translations.literal: The imperial clansmen therefore resented Dong and bitterly reviled him; the emperor too had risen from a princely establishment, but after investigation he did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clansmen therefore hated Dong and bitterly slandered him; the emperor too had come from a princely household, but after inquiry he did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 轉司封員外郎、權三司度支判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel's Enfeoffment Bureau and acting Finance Commissioner of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel's Enfeoffment Bureau and made acting Finance Commissioner of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 對便殿稱旨，英宗遂欲進用，大臣忌之，出為江西轉運使。

translations.literal: Appearing at the informal hall he pleased the emperor; Yingzong wished to promote him, but great ministers envied him and he was sent out as transport commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When he answered at the informal hall he pleased the emperor, and Yingzong wished to advance him; the chief ministers envied him, and he was sent out as Jiangxi transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 江西薦饑，徵民積歲賦，洞為奏免之。

translations.literal: Jiangxi suffered successive famine, and accumulated years of tax were levied on the people; Dong memorialized for exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi suffered repeated famine, yet back taxes of many years were being collected; Dong memorialized to have them remitted.

sentences.zh: 又民輸綢絹不中度者，舊責以滿匹，洞命計尺寸輸錢，民便之。

translations.literal: Also, when the people delivered silk that did not meet standard measure, old practice charged them for a full bolt; Dong ordered payment by measured length in cash, and the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: When silk delivered by the people fell short of standard width, the old rule charged them for a full bolt; Dong ordered payment by measured length in cash, which greatly eased the burden.

sentences.zh: 移淮南轉運使，轉工部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Huainan transport commissioner and promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Huainan transport commissioner and promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 淮南地不宜麥，民艱於所輸，洞復命輸錢，官為糴麥，不逾時而足。

translations.literal: Huainan land was unsuited to wheat, and the people struggled with what they had to deliver; Dong again ordered cash payment; the government bought wheat, and in no time supplies were full.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan was ill suited to wheat, and the people had difficulty meeting their deliveries; Dong again allowed payment in cash while the government purchased wheat, and supplies were soon complete.

sentences.zh: 洞在棣時，夢人稱敕召者，既出，如拜官然，顧視旌旗吏卒羅於庭。

translations.literal: When Dong was at Dizhou, he dreamed someone proclaiming an edict summoning him; going out it was like receiving an appointment, and looking back he saw banners, flags, clerks, and soldiers arrayed in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: While at Dizhou, Dong dreamed that someone proclaimed an edict summoning him; when he went out it was as if he were being appointed to office, and behind him banners, flags, clerks, and soldiers filled the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 至是，夢之如初。

translations.literal: Now he dreamed it again as before.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he dreamed the same thing again.

sentences.zh: 自以年不能永，教諸子部分家事。

translations.literal: He felt his years would not be long and instructed his sons to divide household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Believing his life would not be long, he instructed his sons on how to divide the household affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 李仕衡

translations.literal: Li Shixing
translations.idiomatic: Li Shixing

sentences.zh: 李仕衡，字天均，秦州成紀人，後家京兆府。

translations.literal: Li Shixing, styled Tianjun, was a native of Chengji in Qinzhou and later settled in Jingzhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shixing, courtesy name Tianjun, was from Chengji in Qinzhou and later made his home in Jingzhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，調鄠縣主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of E County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of E County.

sentences.zh: 田重進守京兆，命仕衡鞫死囚五人，活者四人。

translations.literal: Tian Chongjin defended Jingzhao and ordered Shixing to try five death-row prisoners; four lived.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Chongjin was defending Jingzhao, he ordered Shixing to retry five condemned prisoners; four were spared.

sentences.zh: 重進即其家謂曰：「子有陰施，此門當高大之。」

translations.literal: Chongjin went at once to his home and said: "You have done hidden good; this gate ought to be raised high."
translations.idiomatic: Chongjin went straight to his home and said, "You have done secret good; this gate is destined to rise high."

sentences.zh: 徙知彭山縣，就加大理評事，遷光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred as magistrate of Pengshan County, concurrently promoted to reviewing officer in the Court of Judicial Review, and promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Pengshan County, concurrently made reviewing officer in the Court of Judicial Review, and promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 父益，以不法誅，仕衡亦坐除名。
