translations.literal: His father Yi was executed for unlawful conduct, and Shixing also was punished and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was executed for unlawful conduct, and Shixing was also dismissed from office as punishment.

sentences.zh: 後會赦，寇準薦其材，盡復其官，領渭橋輦運，通判邠州，再遷秘書丞，徙知劍州。

translations.literal: Later an amnesty came; Kou Zhun recommended his talent; all his offices were restored; he headed Weiqiao cart transport, served as vice-prefect of Binzhou, was again promoted to secretary of the Palace Secretariat, and was transferred as prefect of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when an amnesty was proclaimed, Kou Zhun recommended his ability and all his offices were restored; he headed Weiqiao cart transport, served as vice-prefect of Binzhou, was promoted again to secretary of the Palace Secretariat, and was transferred to prefect of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 王均反，仕衡度州兵不足守，即棄城焚芻粟，輦金帛東守劍門。

translations.literal: Wang Jun rebelled; Shixing judged the prefecture's troops insufficient to hold it, immediately abandoned the city, burned fodder and grain, and transported gold and silk east to hold Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun rebelled, Shixing judged the prefecture's troops too few to hold the city; he abandoned it at once, burned fodder and grain, and moved gold and silk east to defend Jianmen.

sentences.zh: 既而賊陷漢州，攻劍州，州空無所資，即趨劍門。

translations.literal: Soon the rebels took Hanzhou and attacked Jianzhou; the prefecture was empty with no resources, and he hastened to Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels captured Hanzhou and attacked Jianzhou; with the prefecture empty and without supplies, he hurried to Jianmen.

sentences.zh: 仕衡預招賊眾，得千餘人，待之不疑。

translations.literal: Shixing had beforehand recruited the rebel troops, getting more than a thousand, and treated them without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing had beforehand recruited more than a thousand of the rebel troops and treated them without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 賊將至，與鈐轄裴臻迎擊之，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: When the rebels were about to arrive, together with Military Controller Pei Zhen he went out to meet and attack them, beheading several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were about to arrive, he and Military Controller Pei Zhen went out to meet them in battle and beheaded several thousand.

sentences.zh: 乃乘驛入奏，擢尚書度支員外郎，賜服緋魚。

translations.literal: Then riding post horses he entered to report; he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue's Finance Bureau and bestowed a purple robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode post horses to the capital to report; he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue's Finance Bureau and granted the purple robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 已而使者言仕衡嘗棄城，降監虔州稅。

translations.literal: Soon an envoy reported that Shixing had once abandoned the city, and he was demoted to supervisor of Ganzhou tax.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an envoy reported that Shixing had once abandoned the city, and he was demoted to supervisor of Ganzhou tax collection.

sentences.zh: 召還，判三司鹽鐵勾院。

translations.literal: He was recalled and made president of the Salt and Iron Audit Bureau of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he was made president of the Salt and Iron Audit Bureau of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 度支使梁鼎言：「商人入粟於邊，率高其直，而售以解鹽。

translations.literal: Finance Commissioner Liang Ding said: "Merchants deliver grain to the border at greatly inflated prices and sell it for monopoly salt vouchers.
translations.idiomatic: Finance Commissioner Liang Ding said, "Merchants deliver grain to the border at greatly inflated prices and receive monopoly salt vouchers in return.

sentences.zh: 商利益博，國用日耗。

translations.literal: Merchant profit is vast, and state revenues daily dwindle.
translations.idiomatic: The merchants' profits are enormous, and state revenues dwindle by the day.

sentences.zh: 請調丁夫轉粟，而輦鹽諸州，官自鬻之，歲可得緡錢三十萬。」

translations.literal: I request corvée labor to transport grain and cart salt to the various prefectures for official sale—yearly one can obtain three hundred thousand strings of cash."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that corvée labor be mobilized to transport grain, that salt be carted to the prefectures and sold by the state, and that this yield three hundred thousand strings of cash each year."

sentences.zh: 仕衡曰：「安邊無大於息民，今不得已而調歛之，又增以轉粟輓鹽之役，欲其不困，何可得哉！」

translations.literal: Shixing said: "Nothing secures the border more than giving the people rest; now we must levy them, yet we add grain transport and salt haulage—how can we expect them not to suffer!"
translations.idiomatic: Shixing said, "Nothing secures the border more than easing the people; now we levy them because we must, yet we add grain transport and salt haulage on top—how can they not be distressed!"

sentences.zh: 不聽，遂行鼎議，而關中大擾。

translations.literal: He was not heeded; Ding's proposal was carried out, and Guanzhong was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not taken; Ding's plan was implemented, and Guanzhong was thrown into great turmoil.

sentences.zh: 乃罷鼎度支使，以仕衡為荊湖北路轉運使，徙陝西。

translations.literal: Then Ding was removed as Finance Commissioner; Shixing was made transport commissioner of Northern Jing-Hu Circuit and transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was then removed as Finance Commissioner, and Shixing was made transport commissioner of Northern Jing-Hu Circuit and transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 初，歲出內帑緡錢三十萬，助陝西軍費。

translations.literal: At first the court yearly disbursed three hundred thousand strings from the inner treasury to aid Shaanxi military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the court had disbursed three hundred thousand strings from the inner treasury each year to support Shaanxi military expenses.

sentences.zh: 仕衡言歲計可自辦，遂罷給。

translations.literal: Shixing said yearly accounts could be self-managed, and the aid was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing said the yearly budget could be managed locally, and the subsidy was abolished.

sentences.zh: 真宗謁陵寢，因幸洛，仕衡獻粟五十萬斛，又以三十萬斛饋京西。

translations.literal: Zhenzong visited the imperial tombs and then proceeded to Luoyang; Shixing presented five hundred thousand bushels of grain and also supplied three hundred thousand bushels to Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong visited the imperial tombs and then proceeded to Luoyang, Shixing presented five hundred thousand bushels of grain and sent another three hundred thousand bushels to Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以為材，召為度支副使。

translations.literal: The court considered him talented and summoned him as Vice Finance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court regarded him as capable and summoned him to serve as Vice Finance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上言：「關右既弛鹽禁，而永興、同華耀四州猶率賣鹽，年額錢請減十之四。」

translations.literal: He submitted: "Though salt restrictions in the region west of the pass had been relaxed, Yongxing, Tong, Hua, and Yao prefectures still routinely sold salt; I request reducing the yearly quota by four-tenths."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted, "Although salt restrictions in the Guan region west had been relaxed, Yongxing, Tong, Hua, and Yao prefectures still routinely sold salt; I ask that the yearly quota be reduced by four-tenths."

sentences.zh: 詔悉除之。

translations.literal: An edict removed it all.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished the quotas entirely.

sentences.zh: 累遷司封郎中，為河北轉運使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel's Enfeoffment Bureau and served as Hebei transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Director in the Ministry of Personnel's Enfeoffment Bureau and served as Hebei transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又奏罷內帑所助緡錢百萬。

translations.literal: He again memorialized to stop inner treasury aid of one million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: He again memorialized to abolish the inner treasury subsidy of one million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 建言：「河北歲給諸軍帛七十萬，而民艱於得錢，悉預假於里豪，出倍償之息，以是工機之利愈薄。

translations.literal: He proposed: "Hebei yearly supplies seven hundred thousand bolts of cloth to the armies, but the people struggle to get cash and all advance-borrow from local magnates at double-interest repayment—thus profit from textile workshops grows ever thinner.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed, "Hebei supplies seven hundred thousand bolts of cloth to the armies each year, yet the people have difficulty obtaining cash and must borrow in advance from local magnates at double interest—so the profit of the weaving workshops grows ever thinner.

sentences.zh: 方春民不足，請戶給錢，至夏輸帛，則民獲利而官用足矣。

translations.literal: In spring when the people are short, I request paying cash per household; by summer they deliver cloth—then the people gain and official needs are met.
translations.idiomatic: When the people are short in spring, pay them cash by household; let them deliver cloth in summer—then the people profit and official needs are met.

sentences.zh: 詔優其直，仍推其法於天下。

translations.literal: An edict improved the price and extended the method empire-wide.
translations.idiomatic: An edict improved the price paid and extended the method throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 封泰山，獻錢帛、芻糧各十萬，見於行宮，遷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the Mount Tai feng encomium he presented one hundred thousand each in cash, silk, fodder, and grain; appearing at the traveling palace he was promoted to Right Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: At the Mount Tai feng encomium he presented one hundred thousand each in cash, silk, fodder, and grain; received at the traveling palace, he was promoted to Right Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，又助錢帛三十萬，乃命同林特提舉京西、陝西轉運事。

translations.literal: At the Fenyin sacrifice he again contributed three hundred thousand in cash and silk, and was then ordered together with Lin Te to oversee Jingxi and Shaanxi transport affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the Fenyin sacrifice he again contributed three hundred thousand in cash and silk, and was then ordered with Lin Te to oversee Jingxi and Shaanxi transport affairs.

sentences.zh: 權知永興軍，進給事中。

translations.literal: He served as acting military commissioner of Yongxing Army and was promoted to Supervising Censorate Official.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting military commissioner of Yongxing Army and was promoted to Supervising Censorate Official.

sentences.zh: 逾月，以樞密直學士知益州。

translations.literal: Within a month, as Academician in the Privy Council he was made prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was made prefect of Yizhou with the title Academician in the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 頃之，河北闕軍儲，議者以謂仕衡前過助封祀費，真宗聞之，以為河北都轉運使。

translations.literal: Soon Hebei lacked military stores; commentators said Shixing had previously overspent helping the feng sacrifice costs; Zhenzong heard this and made him chief transport commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hebei lacked military stores; critics blamed Shixing for having overspent on the feng sacrifice; when Zhenzong heard this, he made Shixing chief transport commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 駕如亳州，又貢絲錦、縑帛各二十萬。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went to Bozhou, he again offered two hundred thousand each in silk brocade and bolted cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage visited Bozhou, he again presented two hundred thousand each in silk brocade and bolted cloth.

sentences.zh: 後集粟塞下，至鉅萬斛。

translations.literal: Later he gathered grain below the passes, reaching tens of thousands of bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Later he stockpiled grain below the passes, amounting to tens of thousands of bushels.

sentences.zh: 或言粟腐不可食，朝廷遣使取視之，而粟不腐也。

translations.literal: Some said the grain had rotted and was inedible; the court sent an envoy to inspect it, but the grain had not rotted.
translations.idiomatic: Some claimed the grain had spoiled and was inedible; the court sent an envoy to inspect it, but the grain had not spoiled.

sentences.zh: 棣州汙下，苦水患，仕衡奏徙州西北七十里，既而大水沒故城丈餘。

translations.literal: Dizhou was low-lying and suffered from floods; Shixing memorialized to move the prefecture seventy li northwest; soon a great flood submerged the old city by more than one zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Dizhou was low-lying and plagued by floods; Shixing memorialized to move the prefecture seventy li northwest, and soon a great flood submerged the old city to a depth of more than one zhang.

sentences.zh: 南郊，復進錢帛八十萬。

translations.literal: At the southern suburban sacrifice he again presented eight hundred thousand in cash and silk.
translations.idiomatic: At the southern suburban sacrifice he again presented eight hundred thousand in cash and silk.

sentences.zh: 先是，每有大禮，仕衡必以所部供軍物為貢，言者以為不實。

translations.literal: Before this, at every great ritual Shixing always offered military supplies from his circuit as tribute, and critics said it was false.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, at every major ritual Shixing had presented military supplies from his circuit as tribute, and critics claimed the figures were false.

sentences.zh: 仕衡乃條析進六十萬皆上供者，二十萬即其羨餘。

translations.literal: Shixing then itemized: six hundred thousand presented were all for imperial supply; two hundred thousand were his surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing then itemized the matter: six hundred thousand were all for imperial supply, and two hundred thousand came from his surplus.

sentences.zh: 帝不之罪，謂王旦曰：「仕衡應猝有材，人欲以此中之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not punish him and said to Wang Dan: "Shixing has talent for sudden demands; people wish to use this to get at him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not punish him and said to Wang Dan, "Shixing has a gift for meeting sudden demands; people wish to use this against him.

sentences.zh: 然朝廷所須，隨大小即辦，亦其所長也。」

translations.literal: Yet whatever the court needs, large or small, he at once provides—that too is his strength."
translations.idiomatic: Yet whatever the court requires, great or small, he provides at once—that too is his strength."

sentences.zh: 明年旱蝗，發積粟賑民，又移五萬斛濟京西。

translations.literal: The next year drought and locusts struck; he released stored grain to relieve the people and also moved fifty thousand bushels to aid Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when drought and locusts struck, he released stored grain to relieve the people and also sent fifty thousand bushels to aid Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書工部侍郎、權知天雄軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works and served as acting military commissioner of Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works and made acting military commissioner of Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 民有盜瓜傷主者，法當死，仕衡以歲饑，奏貸之。

translations.literal: A man stole melons and injured the owner—the law called for death; because of the year's famine Shixing memorialized to spare him.
translations.idiomatic: When a man stole melons and injured the owner, the law called for death; because of famine that year, Shixing memorialized to spare him.

sentences.zh: 盜起淄、青間，遷刑部侍郎、知青州。

translations.literal: Bandits rose between Zi and Qing; he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose between Zi and Qing, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 前守捕群盜妻子置棘圍中，仕衡至，悉縱罷之使去。

translations.literal: The previous prefect had captured bandits' wives and children and placed them in thorn enclosures; when Shixing arrived he released them all and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: The previous prefect had captured the bandits' wives and children and held them in thorn stockades; when Shixing arrived he released them all and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其徒有梟賊首至者。

translations.literal: Before long some of their followers brought severed bandit heads and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long some of the bandits' followers brought severed heads and presented them.

sentences.zh: 入為三司使，帝作《寬財利論》以賜之。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Commissioner of the Three Offices; the emperor composed "On Easing Fiscal Profit" and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Commissioner of the Three Offices, and the emperor composed "On Easing Fiscal Profit" and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 乃更陝西入粟法，使民得受錢與茶。

translations.literal: Then he revised the Shaanxi grain-delivery law so the people could receive cash and tea.
translations.idiomatic: He then revised the Shaanxi grain-delivery law so that the people could receive cash and tea.

sentences.zh: 舊市羊及木，責吏送京師，而羊多道死，木至湍險處往往漂失，吏至破產不能償。

translations.literal: Formerly when purchasing sheep and timber, clerks were charged to deliver them to the capital; many sheep died on the road; timber at rapid and dangerous places often drifted away; clerks came to ruin unable to compensate.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, when the government purchased sheep and timber, clerks were required to deliver them to the capital; many sheep died on the road, and timber often drifted away at rapids, until clerks were ruined and unable to make compensation.

sentences.zh: 仕衡乃許吏私附羊，免其算，使得補死者；

translations.literal: Shixing then allowed clerks to attach private sheep, exempt from tax, so they could replace the dead;
translations.idiomatic: Shixing then allowed clerks to attach private sheep, exempt from levy, so they could replace those that died;

sentences.zh: 聽民自采木輸官，用入粟法償其直。

translations.literal: he permitted the people to gather timber themselves and deliver it to the government, compensating them by the grain-delivery law.
translations.idiomatic: and he allowed the people to gather timber themselves and deliver it to the government, compensating them under the grain-delivery law.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 仕衡前後管計事二十年，雖才智過人，然素貪，家貲至累钜萬，建大第長安里中，嚴若官府。

translations.literal: Shixing for twenty years before and after managed fiscal affairs; though his talent and wisdom surpassed others, he was by nature greedy; household wealth accumulated to vast sums; he built a great mansion in Chang'an Lane, stern as a government office.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing managed fiscal affairs for some twenty years; though his talent and wit surpassed others, he was by nature greedy, amassed household wealth to vast sums, and built a great mansion in Chang'an Lane as imposing as a government office.

sentences.zh: 子丕緒，蔭補將作監主簿。

translations.literal: His son Pizu, by inherited privilege, was appointed Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pizu entered office by inherited privilege as Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Works.

sentences.zh: 及仕衡歸老，丕緒時為尚書虞部員外郎，請解官就養。

translations.literal: When Shixing retired, Pizu was then Vice Director in the Parks and Gardens Section of the Ministry of Revenue; he requested to resign office and go home to care for his father.
translations.idiomatic: When Shixing retired, Pizu, then Vice Director in the Parks and Gardens Section of the Ministry of Revenue, asked to resign and return home to support his father.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以為郎，故事不許，請削一官，乃聽。

translations.literal: The court held that for a bureau official precedent did not permit this; he asked to forfeit one rank, and then permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court replied that precedent did not allow a bureau official to do so; only when he offered to forfeit one rank was he permitted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，還之。

translations.literal: Before long, it was restored to him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 居十餘年，仕衡死，服除，久之不出。

translations.literal: He remained at home more than ten years; Shixing died; when mourning ended he still did not emerge for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed out of office more than ten years; after Shixing died and his mourning ended, he still did not come forth for a long time.

sentences.zh: 大臣為言，起僉書永興軍節度判官事。

translations.literal: Great ministers spoke on his behalf, and he was raised to serve as drafting secretary and administrative aide for the Yongxing Army command.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers spoke for him, and he was recalled to serve as drafting secretary and administrative aide on the Yongxing Army staff.

sentences.zh: 歷通判永興軍、同州，知解州、興元府、華州，累遷司農卿致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He served in turn as vice-prefect of Yongxing Army and Tongzhou, as prefect of Jiezhou, Xingyuan Prefecture, and Huazhou, rose repeatedly to Minister of Revenue, retired, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as vice-prefect of Yongxing Army and Tongzhou and as prefect of Jiezhou, Xingyuan Prefecture, and Huazhou, rose repeatedly to Minister of Revenue, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 丕緒居官廉靜，不為矯激。

translations.literal: Pizu in office was honest and quiet, and did not put on showy extremes.
translations.idiomatic: Pizu served with integrity and restraint, never given to ostentatious display.

sentences.zh: 家多圖書，集歷代石刻，為數百卷藏之。

translations.literal: His household had many books and scrolls; he collected stone inscriptions from successive dynasties into several hundred scrolls and stored them.
translations.idiomatic: His household held many books, and he assembled stone inscriptions from successive dynasties into several hundred scrolls for his collection.

sentences.zh: 李溥，河南人。

translations.literal: Li Pu was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Pu was from Henan.

sentences.zh: 初為三司小吏，陰狡多智數。

translations.literal: At first he was a petty clerk in the Three Offices; secretive, cunning, and full of schemes.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a petty clerk in the Three Offices—secretive, cunning, and full of schemes.

sentences.zh: 時天下新定，太宗厲精政事，嘗論及財賦，欲有所更革，引三司吏二十七人對便殿，問以職事。

translations.literal: At the time the realm had just been settled; Emperor Taizong applied himself diligently to government affairs, once discussed revenue and wished to make reforms, and summoned twenty-seven Three Offices clerks to the Privy Hall to question them on their duties.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm had just been settled, Emperor Taizong applied himself diligently to government, once discussed revenue and wished to reform it, and summoned twenty-seven Three Offices clerks to the Privy Hall to question them about their duties.

sentences.zh: 溥詢其目，請退而條上。

translations.literal: Pu asked the scope of the inquiry and requested to withdraw and submit items in order.
translations.idiomatic: Pu asked what topics were wanted and requested leave to withdraw and submit a written list.

sentences.zh: 命至中書，列七十一事以聞，四十四事即日行之，餘下三司議可否。

translations.literal: Ordered to the Secretariat, he listed seventy-one matters for report; forty-four were put into effect that same day, and the rest were sent down to the Three Offices to discuss whether they should be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to the Secretariat, he listed seventy-one items for the throne; forty-four took effect that same day, and the rest were referred to the Three Offices for discussion.

sentences.zh: 於是帝以溥等為能，語輔臣曰：「朕嘗諭陳恕等，如溥輩雖無學，至於金穀利害，必能究知本末，宜假以色辭，誘令開陳。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor regarded Pu and the others as capable and said to the chief ministers: "I once instructed Chen Shu and the others that men like Pu, though without learning, in matters of grain and coin profit and loss can certainly investigate root and branch; they should be approached with kind words to induce them to speak openly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then judged Pu and the others capable and told the chief ministers, "I once told Chen Shu and the others that men like Pu, though without formal learning, can surely get to the bottom of fiscal profit and loss, and should be drawn out with courteous words.

sentences.zh: 而恕等強愎自用，莫肯詢問。」

translations.literal: But Shu and the others were obstinate and self-willed, and none would inquire."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shu and the others were stubborn and self-willed and would not inquire."

sentences.zh: 呂端對曰：「耕當問奴，織當問婢。」

translations.literal: Lü Duan replied: "To plow one should ask the slave; to weave one should ask the maid."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Duan replied, "To plow, ask the farmhand; to weave, ask the maid."

sentences.zh: 寇準曰：「孔子入太廟，每事問。

translations.literal: Kou Zhun said: "When Confucius entered the Grand Temple, he asked about everything.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun said, "When Confucius entered the Grand Temple, he asked about everything.

sentences.zh: 蓋以貴下賤，先有司之義也。」

translations.literal: Surely it is the principle of the noble deferring to the lowly and letting those who hold office go first."
translations.idiomatic: Surely that is the principle of the noble deferring to the lowly and letting those in charge go first."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，悉擢溥等以官，賜錢幣有差。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this right, promoted Pu and the others to office, and bestowed cash and coin in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, promoted Pu and the others to office, and bestowed cash and coin in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 溥為左侍禁、提點三司孔目官，請著內外百官諸軍奉祿為定式。

translations.literal: Pu served as Left Attendant Guard and Supervisor of the Three Offices Registry Clerk, and requested that the salaries of all civil and military officials and all armies be set as fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Pu served as Left Attendant Guard and Supervisor of the Three Offices Registry Clerk and asked that the salaries of civil and military officials and all armies be fixed by regulation.

sentences.zh: 加閤門祗候。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Gate Liaison Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed Gate Liaison Officer.

sentences.zh: 催運陝西糧草，赴清遠軍，還，提舉在京倉草場，勾當北作坊。

translations.literal: He pressed the transport of grain and fodder in Shaanxi to Qingyuan Army; on return he supervised the capital granaries and fodder yards and managed the Northern Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the transport of grain and fodder in Shaanxi to Qingyuan Army; on his return he supervised the capital granaries and fodder yards and managed the Northern Workshops.

sentences.zh: 齊州大水，壞民廬舍，欲徙州城，未決，命溥往視，遂徙城而還。

translations.literal: A great flood in Qizhou destroyed the people's houses; the prefecture wished to move the city but had not decided; Pu was ordered to inspect the site, moved the city, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When a great flood in Qizhou destroyed people's houses, officials wished to move the prefectural seat but had not decided; Pu was sent to inspect the site, moved the city, and returned.

sentences.zh: 又與李仕衡使陝西，增酒榷緡錢歲二十五萬。

translations.literal: He also went with Li Shixing as envoy to Shaanxi and increased the annual wine monopoly revenue by two hundred fifty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: He also went with Li Shixing on a mission to Shaanxi and raised the annual wine monopoly revenue by two hundred fifty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 三遷崇儀使。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Commissioner of Ceremonial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted three times, he became Commissioner of Ceremonial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 景德中，茶法既弊，命與林特、劉承珪更定法，募人入金帛京師，入芻粟塞下，與東南茶皆倍其數，即以溥制置江淮等路茶鹽礬稅兼發運事，使推行之。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era, when the tea law had already grown defective, he was ordered with Lin Te and Liu Chenggui to revise the law: men were recruited to bring gold and silk to the capital and fodder and grain to the frontier, and in each case they received twice the amount in tea from the southeast; Pu was then made Commissioner to oversee tea, salt, alum, and tax affairs on the Jiang-Huai and other circuits together with transport duties, and sent to put the law into effect.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingde era, when the tea law had already broken down, he was ordered with Lin Te and Liu Chenggui to revise it: recruits brought gold and silk to the capital and fodder and grain to the frontier, receiving twice the amount in southeast tea; Pu was then made Commissioner to oversee Jiang-Huai and other circuits' tea, salt, alum, and tax affairs together with transport, and sent to enforce the new law.

sentences.zh: 歲課緡錢，果增其舊，特等皆受賞。

translations.literal: Annual revenue in strings of cash indeed increased over the old amount, and Te and the others all received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Annual revenue in strings of cash did increase over the old level, and Te and the others were all rewarded.

sentences.zh: 溥時已為發運副使，遷為使，仍改西京作坊使。

translations.literal: Pu was then already Vice Commissioner of Transport; he was promoted to Commissioner and also made Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was then Vice Commissioner of Transport; he was promoted to Commissioner and also made Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops.

sentences.zh: 然茶法行之數年，課復損於舊。

translations.literal: Yet after the tea law had been in force several years, revenue again fell below the old level.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after several years under the tea law, revenue again dropped below the old level.

sentences.zh: 江、淮歲運米輸京師，舊止五百餘萬斛，至溥乃增至六百萬，而諸路猶有餘畜。

translations.literal: The Jiang and Huai annually transported grain to the capital; formerly it stopped at a little more than five million hu, but under Pu it rose to six million, and the circuits still had surplus stores.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang and Huai annually shipped grain to the capital; formerly the total stopped at a little over five million hu, but under Pu it rose to six million, and the circuits still had surplus stores.

sentences.zh: 高郵軍新開湖水散漫多風濤，溥令漕舟東下者還過泗州，因載石輸湖中，積為長堤，自是舟行無患。

translations.literal: In Gaoyou Army the newly opened lake waters spread wide and were troubled by wind and waves; Pu ordered grain barges returning east to pass by Sizhou, load stone there, and deposit it in the lake until it formed a long dike; from then on boats passed without trouble.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaoyou Army the newly opened lake spread wide and was troubled by wind and waves; Pu ordered eastbound grain barges returning upstream to pass by Sizhou, load stone, and deposit it in the lake until it formed a long dike, after which boats passed without trouble.

sentences.zh: 累遷北作坊使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Commissioner of the Northern Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Commissioner of the Northern Workshops.

sentences.zh: 時營建玉清昭應宮，溥與丁謂相表裏，盡括東南巧匠遣詣京，且多致奇木怪石，以傅會帝意。

translations.literal: At the time the "Palace of Jade Clarity and Responding Splendor" was under construction; Pu and Ding Wei worked in concert, rounding up skilled craftsmen from the southeast and sending them to the capital, and moreover procuring many strange trees and odd stones to suit the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: While the "Palace of Jade Clarity and Responding Splendor" was being built, Pu and Ding Wei worked hand in glove, rounding up skilled craftsmen from the southeast for the capital and procuring many strange trees and odd stones to suit the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 建安軍鑄玉皇聖祖，溥典其事，丁謂言溥蔬食者周歲，而溥亦數奏祥應，遂以為迎奉聖像都監、領順州刺史，遷獎州團練使。

translations.literal: At Jian'an Army the Jade Emperor Holy Ancestor was cast; Pu directed the work; Ding Wei said Pu had eaten only vegetables for a full year, and Pu also repeatedly memorialized auspicious responses; he was then made Director General for Welcoming the Holy Image and concurrently Prefect of Shunzhou, and promoted to Military Commissioner of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jade Emperor Holy Ancestor was cast at Jian'an Army, Pu directed the work; Ding Wei reported that Pu had eaten only vegetables for a full year, and Pu also repeatedly memorialized auspicious signs; he was then made Director General for Welcoming the Holy Image and concurrently Prefect of Shunzhou, and promoted to Military Commissioner of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 溥自言江、淮歲入茶，視舊額增五百七十餘萬斤。

translations.literal: Pu himself said that annual tea receipts from the Jiang and Huai exceeded the old quota by more than five million seven hundred thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: Pu himself reported that annual tea receipts from the Jiang and Huai exceeded the old quota by more than five million seven hundred thousand jin.

sentences.zh: 並言，漕舟舊以使臣若軍大將，人掌一綱，多侵盜，自溥並三綱為一，以三人共主之，使更相司察。

translations.literal: He also said that formerly on grain barges envoys or army generals each controlled one convoy and often embezzled; since Pu merged three convoys into one and had three men jointly in charge, they were made to watch one another.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that formerly envoys or army generals each controlled one convoy on the grain barges and often embezzled; Pu merged three convoys into one and put three men jointly in charge so they would watch one another.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符九年，初運米一百二十五萬石，才失二百石。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, on the first transport of 1.25 million shi of grain, only two hundred shi were lost.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the first shipment of 1.25 million shi of grain lost only two hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 會溥當代，詔留再任，特遷宮苑使。

translations.literal: When Pu's term was due to end, an edict kept him for another appointment, and he was specially promoted to Commissioner of the Palace Parks.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu's term was due to end, an edict kept him for another appointment and he was specially promoted to Commissioner of the Palace Parks.

sentences.zh: 初，譙縣尉陳齊論榷茶法，溥薦齊任京官，御史中丞王嗣宗方判吏部銓，言齊豪民子，不可用。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qiao County Assistant Chen Qi had discussed the tea monopoly law; Pu recommended Qi for a capital office, but Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Sizong, then presiding over the Ministry of Personnel roster, said Qi was the son of a powerful local family and could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qiao County Assistant Chen Qi had discussed the tea monopoly law; Pu recommended Qi for a capital office, but Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Sizong, then presiding over the Ministry of Personnel roster, said Qi was the son of a powerful local family and was unfit for appointment.

sentences.zh: 真宗以問執政，馮拯對曰：「若用有材，豈限貧富。」

translations.literal: Zhenzong asked the chief ministers; Feng Zheng replied: "If one appoints for talent, why should wealth or poverty limit it?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong asked the chief ministers; Feng Zheng replied, "If one appoints for talent, why should wealth or poverty matter?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What you say is right."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What you say is right."

sentences.zh: 因稱溥畏慎小心，言事未嘗不中利害，以故任之益不疑。

translations.literal: He then praised Pu as cautious and careful, saying his memorials never missed profit and loss in their import, and for this reason entrusted him ever more without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: He then praised Pu as cautious and careful, saying his memorials never missed the mark on profit and loss, and for that reason entrusted him ever more without doubt.

sentences.zh: 然溥久專利權，內倚丁謂，所言輒聽。

translations.literal: Yet Pu for long monopolized fiscal power, relied inward on Ding Wei, and whatever he said was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Pu had long monopolized fiscal power, relied inward on Ding Wei, and whatever he said was heeded.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗語執政曰：「群臣上書論事，法官輒沮之，云非有大益，無改舊章，然則何以廣言路。」

translations.literal: The emperor once told the chief ministers: "When ministers submit memorials discussing affairs, the legal officers always obstruct them, saying that unless there is great benefit there should be no change to old statutes—then how is the path of remonstrance to be broadened?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told the chief ministers, "When ministers submit memorials on policy, legal officers always obstruct them, saying that unless there is great benefit old statutes should not be changed—then how is the path of remonstrance to be broadened?"

sentences.zh: 王旦對曰：「法制數更，則詔令牴牾，故重於變易。」

translations.literal: Wang Dan replied: "If laws and institutions are changed repeatedly, then edicts contradict one another, and therefore change is treated as weighty."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan replied, "If laws and institutions are changed repeatedly, edicts contradict one another, and therefore change is treated as weighty."

sentences.zh: 因言：「溥嘗請盜販茶鹽者贓仗皆沒官，已可之矣。」

translations.literal: He added: "Pu once requested that the illicit goods of smugglers of tea and salt all be confiscated by the state, and this had already been approved."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Pu once requested that the illicit goods of smugglers of tea and salt all be confiscated by the state, and this had already been approved."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此特畏溥之強，不敢退卻，自今雖小吏言，亦宜詳究行之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This was simply fear of Pu's force and not daring to draw back; from now on, even if a petty clerk speaks, it should be examined in detail and put into effect."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That was simply fear of Pu's force and not daring to draw back; from now on, even if a petty clerk speaks, it should be examined in detail and put into effect."

sentences.zh: 胡則，字子正，婺州永康人。

translations.literal: Hu Ze, styled Zizheng, was a man of Yongkang in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ze, courtesy name Zizheng, was from Yongkang in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 果敢有材氣。

translations.literal: He was resolute and daring, with talent and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He was resolute and daring, with talent and force of character.

sentences.zh: 以進士起家，補許田縣尉，再調憲州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Having entered official life through the jinshi examination, he was appointed magistrate of Xutian County, then was transferred to serve as recorder-assistant in Xian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as a jinshi, was appointed magistrate of Xutian County, and was later transferred to recorder-assistant in Xian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時靈、夏用兵，轉運使索湘命則部送芻糧，為一月計。

translations.literal: At the time troops were engaged at Ling and Xia; Transport Commissioner Suo Xiang ordered Ze to escort forage and grain, calculated for one month.
translations.idiomatic: When campaigns were underway at Lingzhou and Xia, Transport Commissioner Suo Xiang ordered Ze to convoy fodder and grain—enough, he reckoned, for one month.

sentences.zh: 則曰：「為百日備，尚恐不支，奈何為一月邪？」

translations.literal: Ze said: "To prepare for a hundred days one still fears it will not suffice—how can one plan for only a month?"
translations.idiomatic: Ze said, "Even a hundred days' provision may not be enough—how can we budget for a single month?"

sentences.zh: 湘懼無以給，遣則遂入奏。

translations.literal: Xiang feared he could not supply it and sent Ze at once to enter court and report.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful that he could not meet the demand, Xiang sent Ze to the capital to report directly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗因問以邊策，對稱旨，顧左右曰：「州縣豈乏人？」

translations.literal: Taizong thereupon questioned him on frontier strategy; his answers pleased the emperor, who turning to those beside him said: "Are prefectures and counties truly short of men?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong questioned him on frontier strategy; his answers pleased the emperor, who turned to those at his side and said, "Are there really no capable men in the counties and prefectures?"

sentences.zh: 命記姓名中書。

translations.literal: He ordered his name recorded at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Ze's name taken down at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後李繼隆討賊，久不解，湘語則曰：「微子幾敗我事。」

translations.literal: Later Li Jilong campaigned against bandits and could not settle matters for a long time; Xiang said to Ze: "But for you I would nearly have ruined the affair."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Li Jilong's campaign against the rebels dragged on without resolution, Xiang told Ze, "But for you I would nearly have ruined everything."

sentences.zh: 一日，繼隆移文轉運司曰：「兵且深入，糧有繼乎？」

translations.literal: One day Jilong sent a dispatch to the transport office saying: "The army is about to penetrate deep—will grain supplies continue?"
translations.idiomatic: One day Jilong sent the transport office a dispatch asking, "The army is about to press deep inland—will provisions keep coming?"

sentences.zh: 則告湘曰：「彼師老將歸，欲以糧乏為辭耳，姑以有餘報之。」

translations.literal: Ze told Xiang: "Their army is weary and about to return; they only wish to use lack of grain as a pretext—reply for the moment that supplies are ample."
translations.idiomatic: Ze told Xiang, "Their troops are weary and ready to withdraw—they only want a pretext of grain shortage. Tell them for now that supplies are ample."

sentences.zh: 已而果為則所料。

translations.literal: Before long matters turned out exactly as Ze had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Events soon bore out Ze's judgment.

sentences.zh: 湘為河北轉運使，奏改秘書省著作佐郎、僉書貝州觀察判官事。

translations.literal: When Xiang became transport commissioner of Hebei, he memorialized to change Ze's post to Assistant Compiler in the Secretariat and concurrent signing officer on the staff of the Beizhou observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang became Hebei transport commissioner, he memorialized to appoint Ze Assistant Compiler in the Secretariat and concurrent staff officer to the Beizhou observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 後以太常博士提舉兩浙榷茶，就知睦州，徙溫州。

translations.literal: Later, as Doctor of the Imperial Sacrifices, he superintended the tea monopoly in the Two Zhes; he took up concurrent appointment as prefect of Muzhou and was transferred to Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Doctor of the Imperial Sacrifices, he oversaw the tea monopoly in the Two Zhes, was given concurrent appointment as prefect of Muzhou, and was then transferred to Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，提舉江南路銀銅場、鑄錢監，得吏所匿銅數萬斤，吏懼且死，則曰：「馬伏波哀重囚而縱之，吾豈重貨而輕數人之生乎？」

translations.literal: After more than a year he superintended the silver and copper yards and coin-minting offices on the Jiangnan circuit; officials' hidden copper of tens of thousands of jin was discovered; the clerks feared death; Ze said: "General Who Pacifies the Waves Ma Yuan pitied serious offenders and released them—would I value goods and slight the lives of several men?"
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he oversaw the Jiangnan circuit's silver and copper yards and mints and uncovered tens of thousands of jin of copper hidden by clerks. They feared execution. Ze said, "Ma Yuan pitied serious offenders and let them go—would I prize copper and treat several men's lives as light?"

sentences.zh: 籍為羨餘，不之罪。

translations.literal: It was entered as surplus revenue; they were not punished.
translations.idiomatic: The copper was entered as surplus revenue, and the clerks went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 改江、淮制置發運使，累遷尚書戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to Jiang-Huai Commissioner for Fiscal Affairs and Transport, and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Jiang-Huai Commissioner for Fiscal Affairs and Transport and rose in stages to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 真宗幸亳還，擢三司度支副使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong returned from his visit to Bozhou, Ze was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Budget in the Finance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong returned from his visit to Bozhou, Ze was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Budget in the Finance Commission.

sentences.zh: 初，丁謂舉進士，客許田，則厚遇之，謂貴顯，故則驟進用。

translations.literal: At first, when Ding Wei passed the jinshi examination, he lodged as a guest in Xutian; Ze treated him generously; when Wei rose to high rank, Ze was therefore swiftly promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when Ding Wei passed the jinshi and stayed in Xutian as a guest, Ze treated him warmly; when Ding later rose to eminence, Ze's own rapid advancement followed.

sentences.zh: 至是，謂罷政事，出則為京西轉運使，遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: At this time Ding was removed from the council; Ze went out to serve as transport commissioner of Jingxi and was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding was dismissed from the council, Ze was sent out as Jingxi transport commissioner and promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 部內民訛言相驚，至遣使安撫乃定。

translations.literal: Within his jurisdiction the people alarmed one another with false rumors, until envoys were dispatched to reassure them and order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread panic among the people under his jurisdiction, and only after envoys were sent to reassure them did order return.

sentences.zh: 坐是，徙廣西路轉運使。

translations.literal: For this he was transferred to serve as transport commissioner of the Guangxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was transferred to Guangxi transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 有番舶遭風至瓊州，且告食乏，不能去。

translations.literal: A foreign merchant ship, struck by wind, reached Qiongzhou and reported that food was lacking and that it could not depart.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign merchant vessel driven by storm reached Qiongzhou and reported that it was short of food and could not leave.

sentences.zh: 則命貸錢三百萬，吏白夷人狡詐，又風波不可期。

translations.literal: Ze ordered three million in cash lent; clerks reported that the barbarians were cunning and deceitful, and that wind and waves were unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: Ze ordered three million in cash lent to them. His staff warned that the foreigners were cunning and that winds and seas were unreliable.

sentences.zh: 則曰：「彼以急難投我，可拒而不與邪？」

translations.literal: Ze said: "They come to us in urgent distress—can we refuse and not help?"
translations.idiomatic: Ze said, "They come to us in distress—can we turn them away and refuse?"

sentences.zh: 已而償所貸如期。

translations.literal: In time they repaid what had been lent exactly on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: In time they repaid the loan on schedule.

sentences.zh: 又按宜州重辟十九人，為辨活者九人。

translations.literal: He also reviewed serious capital cases in Yizhou involving nineteen persons and secured acquittal or commutation for nine.
translations.idiomatic: He also reviewed capital cases in Yizhou involving nineteen people and secured a reprieve for nine.

sentences.zh: 復為發運使，累遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: He again served as transport commissioner and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as transport commissioner and rose to Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，坐丁謂黨，降知信州，徙福州，以右諫議大夫知杭州。

translations.literal: Early in the Qianxing era, implicated as a member of Ding Wei's faction, he was demoted to prefect of Xinzhou, transferred to Fuzhou, and appointed Right Remonstrance Official with concurrent prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianxing era, implicated in Ding Wei's faction, he was demoted to prefect of Xinzhou, transferred to Fuzhou, and made Right Remonstrance Official with concurrent appointment as prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 入權吏部流內銓，坐失舉，復為太常少卿、知池州。

translations.literal: He entered the capital to serve as acting director of the Bureau of Personnel Rosters in the Ministry of Personnel; convicted of faulty recommendations, he again became Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as acting head of the Ministry roster bureau; found guilty of faulty recommendations, he was again made Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，復諫議大夫、知永興軍，徙河北都轉運使，以給事中權三司使，通京東西、陝西鹽法，人便之。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the post, he was again made Remonstrance Official and prefect of the Yongxing command, transferred to chief transport commissioner of Hebei, and as Drafting Official served as acting Commissioner of the Finance Commission, harmonizing the salt laws of Eastern and Western Jing and of Shaanxi—the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up his post he was again made Remonstrance Official and prefect of the Yongxing command, then transferred to chief Hebei transport commissioner; as Drafting Official he served as acting Finance Commissioner and unified the salt laws of Eastern and Western Jing and Shaanxi, to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 初，則在河北，殿中侍御史王沿嘗就則假官舟販鹽，又以其子為名祈買酒場。

translations.literal: At first, when Ze was in Hebei, Palace Attendant Censor Wang Yan once borrowed an official boat from Ze to trade in salt, and also used his son's name to petition to purchase a wine franchise.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Ze was in Hebei, Palace Attendant Censor Wang Yan had borrowed an official boat from him to trade in salt and had used his son's name to petition for purchase of a wine franchise.

sentences.zh: 至是，張宗誨擿發之，按驗得實，出則知陳州。

translations.literal: At this time Zhang Zonghui exposed the matter; investigation confirmed the facts, and Ze was sent out as prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhang Zonghui exposed the affair; investigation confirmed it, and Ze was sent out as prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾月，授工部侍郎、集賢院學士。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and Academician in the Hall for Assembling Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and Academician in the Hall for Assembling Worthies.

sentences.zh: 劉隨上疏言：「則奸邪貪濫聞天下，比命知池州，不肯行，今以罪去，驟加美職，何以風勸在位？」

translations.literal: Liu Sui submitted a memorial saying: "Ze's wickedness, corruption, and greed are known throughout the realm; recently ordered to serve as prefect of Chizhou, he refused to go; now, though removed for crime, he is suddenly given an honored post—how can this edify and encourage those in office?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sui submitted a memorial saying, "Ze's wickedness and greed are notorious throughout the realm. Recently ordered to Chizhou, he refused to go; now, though dismissed for misconduct, he is suddenly given a fine post—what lesson does this teach those in office?"

sentences.zh: 後徙杭州，再遷兵部侍郎致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Hangzhou, was again promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War and retired, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Hangzhou, rose again to Vice Director in the Ministry of War, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 則無廉名，喜交結，尚風義。

translations.literal: Ze had no reputation for integrity; he liked to cultivate connections and valued personal honor.
translations.idiomatic: Ze had no reputation for integrity, yet he loved to forge connections and prized personal loyalty.

sentences.zh: 丁謂貶崖州，賓客隨散落，獨則間遣人至海上，饋問如平日。

translations.literal: When Ding Wei was banished to Yazhou, his guests scattered with him; only Ze from time to time sent men to the coast with gifts and inquiries as in ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Wei was banished to Yazhou his retainers scattered—but Ze still sent men from time to time to the coast with gifts and greetings, as in ordinary times.

sentences.zh: 在福州時，前守陳絳嘗延蜀人龍昌期為眾人講《易》，得錢十萬。

translations.literal: While in Fuzhou, the former prefect Chen Jiang had once invited the Shu man Long Changqi to lecture on the Changes for the assembled company and received a hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: While Ze was in Fuzhou, the former prefect Chen Jiang had once invited the Shu scholar Long Changqi to lecture on the Changes before a gathering and was paid a hundred thousand in cash.

sentences.zh: 絳既坐罪，遂自成都械昌期至。

translations.literal: After Jiang was convicted, Long Changqi was shackled and brought from Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiang was convicted, Changqi was shackled and brought from Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 則破械，館以賓禮，出俸錢為償之。

translations.literal: Ze removed the shackles, lodged him with the rites due a guest, and paid out his official salary to settle the debt for him.
translations.idiomatic: Ze had the shackles removed, received him as an honored guest, and paid the debt from his own salary.

sentences.zh: 昌期者，嘗注《易》、《詩》、《書》、《論語》、《孝經》、《陰符經》、《老子》，其說詭誕穿鑿，至詆斥周公。

translations.literal: As for Changqi, he had annotated the Changes, the Odes, the Documents, the Analects, the Classic of Filial Piety, the Yin Fu Classic, and the Laozi; his interpretations were bizarre, forced, and contrived, going so far as to revile the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Changqi had written commentaries on the Changes, the Odes, the Documents, the Analects, the Classic of Filial Piety, the Yin Fu Classic, and the Laozi—interpretations far-fetched and forced, going so far as to denounce the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 初用薦者補國子四門助教，文彥博守成都，召置府學，奏改秘書省校書郎，後以殿中丞致仕。

translations.literal: At first, through a recommender, he was appointed Assistant Instructor at the Four Gates of the Directorate of Education; when Wen Yanbo served as defender of Chengdu, he summoned him to the prefectural school, memorialized to change his post to Collator in the Secretariat, and later retired as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Through recommendation he was first appointed Assistant Instructor at the Four Gates of the Directorate of Education. When Wen Yanbo defended Chengdu he summoned him to the prefectural school and memorialized for his appointment as Collator in the Secretariat; later he retired as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 著書百餘卷，嘉祐中，詔取其書。

translations.literal: He authored more than a hundred scrolls of books; in the Jiayou era an edict ordered his writings taken into the collection.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than a hundred scrolls; in the Jiayou era an edict ordered his works collected.

sentences.zh: 昌期時年八十餘，野服自詣京師，賜緋魚，絹百匹。

translations.literal: Changqi was then over eighty; in plain dress he presented himself at the capital and was granted the red fish pouch and a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Changqi was then over eighty. Dressed plainly he traveled to the capital on his own and was granted the red fish insignia and a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修言其異端害道，不當推獎，奪所賜服罷歸，卒。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu said his heterodox teachings harmed the Way and that he should not be promoted and rewarded; the gifts were revoked and he was sent back; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu argued that his heterodox teachings harmed the Way and that he ought not be honored; the gifts were revoked and he was sent home, and he died.

sentences.zh: 薛顏，字彥回，河中萬泉人。

translations.literal: Xue Yan, styled Yanhui, was a native of Wanquan in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yan, courtesy name Yanhui, came from Wanquan in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 舉《三禮》中第，為嘉州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the examination in the Three Rites at the highest level and was appointed revenue officer of Jia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the Three Rites examination and was appointed revenue officer of Jia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 代還引見，太宗顧問之，對稱旨，改將作監丞、監華州酒稅。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, he was granted audience; Taizong questioned him personally; his answers pleased the emperor, and he was changed to Director in the Directorate of Works and supervisor of Huazhou's wine tax.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was granted audience; Taizong questioned him in person and was pleased with his answers, and he was made Director in the Directorate of Works and supervisor of Huazhou's wine tax.

sentences.zh: 以秘書省著作佐郎使夔、峽，疏決刑獄。

translations.literal: As Assistant Compiler in the Secretariat he was dispatched to Kui and Xia to review and decide criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: As Assistant Compiler in the Secretariat he was sent to Kui and Xia to review criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 還，改太子左贊善大夫、知雲安軍，徙渝、閬二州，擢三司鹽鐵判官，河北計置糧草。

translations.literal: On his return he was changed to Left Supervisor in the Eastern Palace and prefect of the Yun'an command, transferred to Yu and Lang prefectures, and promoted to Salt and Iron Commissioner in the Finance Commission to plan forage and grain in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was made Left Supervisor in the Eastern Palace and prefect of the Yun'an command, served in turn at Yu and Lang prefectures, and was promoted to Salt and Iron Commissioner in the Finance Commission to arrange forage and grain in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 初，丁謂招撫溪蠻，有威惠，部人愛之。

translations.literal: At first, when Ding Wei pacified and appeased the Xi Man, he possessed both stern authority and gracious kindness, and the people under his jurisdiction loved him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Wei first pacified the Xi Man he combined stern authority with gracious kindness, and the people under his command loved him.

sentences.zh: 留五年，詔謂自舉代，謂薦顏為峽路轉運使，累遷尚書虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: He remained five years; an edict had Wei recommend his own successor, and Wei recommended Yan as transport commissioner for the Gorge route; he was repeatedly promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in office, an edict directed Ding Wei to name his own successor; Wei recommended Yan as transport commissioner for the Gorge route, and Yan rose in time to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 始，孟氏據蜀，徙夔州於東山，據峽以拒王師，而民居不便也，顏為復其故城。

translations.literal: At first, when the Meng clan held Shu, they moved Kui Prefecture to East Mountain and held the gorges to resist the imperial army, but this was inconvenient for the people; Yan restored the old city for them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Meng clan first held Shu, they had moved Kui Prefecture to East Mountain and held the gorges against the imperial armies, to the people's inconvenience; Yan restored the old city.

sentences.zh: 宜州陳進反，命勾當廣南東、西路轉運司事。

translations.literal: When Chen Jin of Yi Prefecture rebelled, Yan was ordered to oversee affairs of the Eastern and Western Guangnan Transport Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Jin rebelled in Yi Prefecture, Yan was assigned to manage the Eastern and Western Guangnan transport commissions.

sentences.zh: 賊平，遷金部員外郎，改河東轉運使。

translations.literal: When the rebels were suppressed, he was transferred to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Works and made transport commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, he was made Assistant Director in the Ministry of Works and transport commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，徙陝西。

translations.literal: When the emperor performed sacrifices at Fenyin, he was transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Fenyin sacrifices he was transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 河中浮橋歲為水所敗，顏即北岸釃上流為支渠，以殺水怒，因取渠水溉其旁田，民頗利之。

translations.literal: The floating bridge at Hezhong was destroyed by water every year; Yan immediately dammed the upstream on the north bank to form a branch channel that reduced the water's force, then used the channel water to irrigate the fields beside it, greatly benefiting the people.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the floating bridge at Hezhong was wrecked by flood; Yan dammed the upstream on the north bank to cut a branch channel that tamed the current, then used its water to irrigate nearby fields—a great benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 坊州募人煉礬，歲久課益重，至有破產被繫不能償者。

translations.literal: Fang Prefecture recruited people to refine alum; over the years the quota grew heavier, until some went bankrupt and were imprisoned, unable to pay.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Prefecture conscripted people to refine alum; year by year the levy grew heavier, until some families were ruined and their members imprisoned for debts they could not pay.

sentences.zh: 顏奏：「罷坊礬，則晉礬當大售。」

translations.literal: Yan memorialized: "If the Fang alum works are abolished, then Jin alum will sell in great quantities."
translations.idiomatic: Yan memorialized, "If we shut down the Fang alum works, Jin alum will sell in great quantities."

sentences.zh: 後如其策。

translations.literal: Later events proved as his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Later events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 徙河北。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: His next assignment was Hebei.

sentences.zh: 歷知河陽、杭徐州，累遷光祿少卿，以少府監知江寧府。

translations.literal: He served in turn as prefect of Heyang, Hangzhou, and Xuzhou, was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and served as prefect of Jiangning with the title Director of the Directorate of Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Heyang, Hangzhou, and Xuzhou, rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and governed Jiangning as Director of the Directorate of Palace Workshops.

sentences.zh: 邏者晝劫人，反執平人以告。

translations.literal: Patrol guards robbed people in broad daylight, yet seized ordinary citizens instead and reported them as the culprits.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol guards robbed people in broad daylight, then seized innocent bystanders and reported them as the thieves.

sentences.zh: 顏視其色動，曰：「若真盜也。」

translations.literal: Yan looked at their shifting color and said: "You are the real thieves."
translations.idiomatic: Yan watched their faces change and said, "You are the real thieves."

sentences.zh: 械之，果引伏。

translations.literal: He had them shackled, and they indeed confessed.
translations.idiomatic: He had them shackled, and they confessed at once.

sentences.zh: 轉右諫議大夫、知河南府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Remonstrating Grandee and prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Remonstrating Grandee and prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遷給事中。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne, he was promoted to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 丁謂分司西京，以顏雅與善，徙知應天府，又徙耀州。

translations.literal: Ding Wei served at the Western Capital; because Yan was refined and on good terms with him, Yan was transferred to prefect of Yingtian and then to Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei held a post at the Western Capital; because Yan was cultivated and friendly with him, Yan was made prefect of Yingtian and then of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 部有豪姓李甲，結客數十人，號「沒命社」，少不如意，則推一人以死鬥之，積數年，為鄉人患，莫敢發。

translations.literal: In his jurisdiction was a powerful clansman named Li Jia, who gathered dozens of clients in a society called the Society of Those Who Stake Their Lives; if they were slightly displeased, they would push one member into a fight to the death; this went on for years and became a scourge to the countryside, yet no one dared expose them.
translations.idiomatic: In his jurisdiction a powerful clansman named Li Jia gathered dozens of followers into a band called the Society of Those Who Stake Their Lives; at the slightest grievance they would thrust one man into a duel to the death. For years they plagued the countryside, and no one dared denounce them.

sentences.zh: 顏至，大索其黨，會赦當免，特杖甲流海上，餘悉籍於軍。

translations.literal: When Yan arrived, he searched broadly for their gang; an amnesty would have exempted them, but he specially had Jia beaten and exiled to the sea, and registered the rest in the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan arrived he hunted down the whole gang; an amnesty would have spared them, but he had Jia beaten and exiled to the coast by special order, and enrolled the rest in the army.

sentences.zh: 以光祿卿分司西京，卒於家。

translations.literal: As Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments he served at the Western Capital and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments at the Western Capital, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 嘗屬杜衍為墓誌，衍卻之。

translations.literal: He once asked Du Yan to write his tomb inscription; Du Yan declined.
translations.idiomatic: He once asked Du Yan to compose his tomb inscription; Du Yan refused.

sentences.zh: 仁宗聞其事，他日，謂衍曰：「薛顏有醜行，卿不欲志其墓，誠清識也。」

translations.literal: Renzong heard of this; on another day he said to Du Yan: "Xue Yan had disgraceful conduct; you did not wish to write his tomb inscription—truly clear judgment."
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong heard of this, he said to Du Yan on another occasion, "Xue Yan had disgraceful conduct, and you refused to write his tomb inscription—that was truly sound judgment."

sentences.zh: 孫：向，自有傳。

translations.literal: His grandson Xiang has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, his grandson, has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 許元，字子春，宣州宣城人。

translations.literal: Xu Yuan, styled Zichun, was a native of Xuancheng in Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan, courtesy name Zichun, came from Xuancheng in Xuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以父蔭為太廟齋郎，改大理寺丞，累遷國子博士，監在京榷貨務，三門發運判官。

translations.literal: Through his father's privilege he was appointed Temple Acolyte; he was changed to Assistant in the Court of Judicial Review, repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Directorate of Education, supervised the Capital Monopoly Commodity Office, and served as Assistant Transport Commissioner at Sanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's privilege he was appointed Temple Acolyte, then Assistant in the Court of Judicial Review; he rose to Erudite of the Directorate of Education, supervised the Capital Monopoly Commodity Office, and served as Assistant Transport Commissioner at Sanmen.

sentences.zh: 元為吏強敏，尤能商財利。

translations.literal: Yuan as an official was forceful and sharp, and especially adept at calculating profit.
translations.idiomatic: As an official Yuan was forceful and sharp, and especially skilled at turning profit.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，江、淮歲漕不給，京師乏軍儲，參知政事范仲淹薦元可獨倚辦，擢江淮制製置發運判官。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era the yearly grain transport from the Jiang and Huai regions could not meet demand, and the capital lacked military stores; Fan Zhongyan, Vice Grand Councillor, recommended that Yuan alone could be relied on to handle the task, and he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Jiang-Huai System Setup and Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era yearly transport from Jiang and Huai fell short and the capital ran low on military grain; Vice Grand Councillor Fan Zhongyan recommended Yuan as the one man who could solve the crisis, and he was made Vice Commissioner of the Jiang-Huai System Setup and Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 至，則悉發瀕江州縣藏粟，所在留三月食，遠近以次相補，引千餘艘轉漕而西。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he mobilized all stored grain in the counties along the river, leaving three months' supply in each place; near and far supplemented one another in turn, and more than a thousand ships carried grain westward.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he drew out every hoard of grain in the counties along the river, leaving three months' rations locally while nearer and more distant districts replenished one another in sequence; more than a thousand ships carried grain west.

sentences.zh: 未幾，京師足食，朝廷以為任職，就遷副使。

translations.literal: Before long the capital had sufficient food; the court considered him competent and promoted him on the spot to Deputy Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the capital had enough grain; the court judged him equal to the task and promoted him on the spot to Deputy Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遂以尚書主客員外郎為使，進金部，特賜進士出身，遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He was then made External Staff Commissioner with the rank of Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites, advanced to the Gold section, specially granted jinshi status, and promoted to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made External Staff Commissioner with the rank of Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites, advanced to the Gold section, granted jinshi status by special favor, and promoted to Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲與施昌言分行二浙、江南調發軍食。

translations.literal: He once wished to divide with Shi Changyan the requisition of military grain from the Two Zhe and Jiangnan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He once proposed that he and Shi Changyan divide between them the requisition of military grain from the Two Zhe and Jiangnan circuits.

sentences.zh: 仁宗聞之，語輔臣曰：「東南歲比不登，民力匱乏，嘗詔損歲漕百萬石，而元與昌言乃更欲分道而出，是必誅求疲民以自為功，非朕志也。」

translations.literal: Renzong heard of this and told his chief ministers: "The southeast has had successive poor harvests and the people's strength is exhausted; I once ordered a reduction of a million shi in yearly transport, yet Yuan and Changyan now wish to divide routes—this will surely extort and exhaust the people to make their own achievement; it is not my intent."
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong heard of this he told his chief ministers, "The southeast has suffered harvest after harvest of failure and the people are exhausted; I once ordered a million shi cut from yearly transport, yet Yuan and Changyan now want to split the routes—surely they would squeeze the weary people to win credit for themselves. That is not my intent."

sentences.zh: 下詔戒飭。

translations.literal: An edict of warning and restraint was issued.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of admonition was issued.

sentences.zh: 既而元欲專六路財賦，收羨餘以媚三司，憚諸部不從，請以六路轉運司自隸，既可之矣，而轉運使多論其罪，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Then Yuan wished to monopolize the finances of the six circuits, collect surpluses to please the Finance Commission, and, fearing that the various departments would not obey, requested that the six circuit transport commissions be placed directly under him; this was approved, but the transport commissioners mostly denounced his offenses, and the matter was ultimately abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan then sought to monopolize the six circuits' finances, skim surpluses to please the Finance Commission, and—fearing the departments would not comply—asked that the six circuit transport commissions be placed directly under him. Though this was approved, most transport commissioners denounced his abuses, and the plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 擢天章閣待制，再遷郎中，以疾請還。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Awaiting Draft in the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and again to Director, then requested to return home because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Awaiting Draft in the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and again to Director, then asked to retire on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 歷知揚、越、泰州，卒。

translations.literal: He served in turn as prefect of Yang, Yue, and Taizhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Yang, Yue, and Taizhou in succession, then died.

sentences.zh: 元在江、淮十三年，以聚斂刻剝為能，急於進取，多聚珍奇以賂遺京師權貴，尤為王堯臣所知。

translations.literal: Yuan spent thirteen years in Jiang and Huai, taking ability in collection and exaction as merit; eager to advance, he amassed many rare treasures to bribe powerful men in the capital, and was especially favored by Wang Yao Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan spent thirteen years in Jiang and Huai, making a virtue of levying and squeezing; hungry for advancement, he hoarded curiosities to bribe capital magnates, and was especially patronized by Wang Yao Chen.

sentences.zh: 發運使治所在真州，衣冠之求官舟者，日數十輩。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner's headquarters was at Zhen Prefecture; gentry seeking official boats numbered dozens each day.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner's seat was at Zhen Prefecture, and every day dozens of gentry came seeking official boats.

sentences.zh: 元視勢家貴族，立榷巨艦與之；

translations.literal: Yuan, seeing powerful families and nobles, immediately set aside great ships for them under monopoly;
translations.idiomatic: When powerful families and nobles appeared, Yuan immediately reserved great ships for them;

sentences.zh: 即小官惸獨，伺候歲月，有不能得。

translations.literal: but for minor officials alone and isolated, they waited month after month, sometimes unable to obtain one.
translations.idiomatic: but minor officials without backing might wait month after month and still fail to get a boat.

sentences.zh: 人以是憤怨，而元自為以當然，無所愧憚。

translations.literal: People therefore resented and hated him, yet Yuan himself thought it only right and felt no shame or fear.
translations.idiomatic: People resented him bitterly, yet Yuan thought it only proper and felt neither shame nor fear.

sentences.zh: 鍾離瑾

translations.literal: Zhong Lijin
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Lijin.

sentences.zh: 鍾離瑾，字公瑜，廬州合肥人。

translations.literal: Zhong Lijin, styled Gongyu, was a native of Hefei in Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Lijin, courtesy name Gongyu, came from Hefei in Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為簡州推官，以殿中丞通判益州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served as judicial assistant of Jian Prefecture, and as Palace Attendant supervised Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After taking his jinshi degree he served as judicial assistant of Jian Prefecture, then as Palace Attendant and supervisor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 建言：「州郡既上雨，後雖凶旱，多隱之以成前奏，請令監司劾其不實者。」

translations.literal: He submitted a proposal: "After prefectures and counties have reported rain, even if later drought is severe, they often conceal it to match their earlier reports; please order supervisory officials to impeach those whose reports are false."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed, "Once prefectures and counties have reported rain, they often conceal later severe drought to preserve their earlier accounts; let supervisory officials impeach those who file false reports."

sentences.zh: 擢開封府推官，出提點兩浙刑獄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to judicial official of Kaifeng Prefecture and went out as Judicial Intendant for the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to judicial official of Kaifeng Prefecture and sent out as Judicial Intendant for the Two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 衢、潤州饑，聚餓者食之，頗廢農作，請發米二萬斛賑給，家毋過一斛。

translations.literal: Qu and Run prefectures suffered famine; starving people were gathered to be fed, greatly disrupting farm work; he requested the issue of twenty thousand hu of rice for relief, with no household receiving more than one hu.
translations.idiomatic: Qu and Run prefectures were stricken with famine; feeding the starving in assembly badly disrupted farming; he requested twenty thousand hu of rice for relief, with no household given more than one hu.

sentences.zh: 後徙淮南轉運副使，歷京西、河東、河北轉運使，改江淮制置發運使。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Deputy Transport Commissioner of Huainan, served as transport commissioner of Jingxi, Hedong, and Hebei, and was changed to Jiang-Huai System Setup Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Deputy Transport Commissioner of Huainan, served as transport commissioner of Jingxi, Hedong, and Hebei, and was appointed Jiang-Huai System Setup Transport Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 殿直王乙者，請自揚州召伯埭東至瓜州，浚河百二十里，以廢二埭。

translations.literal: Palace Guardsman Wang Yi requested dredging a river one hundred and twenty li from east of Zhaobo Dam in Yangzhou to Guazhou, so as to abolish two dams.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Guardsman Wang Yi proposed dredging a channel one hundred and twenty li from east of Zhaobo Dam in Yangzhou to Guazhou, eliminating two dams in the process.

sentences.zh: 詔瑾規度，以工大不可就，止置閘召伯埭旁，人以為利。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jin to survey the project; he judged the labor too great to complete, and only placed sluice gates beside Zhaobo Dam; the people considered it beneficial.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Jin to assess the plan; he judged the work too vast to finish and settled for sluice gates beside Zhaobo Dam, which the people found beneficial.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書刑部郎中，為三司戶部副使，除龍圖閣待制、權知開封府。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Justice, served as Vice Commissioner of the Revenue Section of the Three Departments, and was appointed Gentleman Awaiting Orders in the Dragon Diagram Hall with acting authority over Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Director in the Ministry of Justice, became Vice Commissioner of the Three Departments' Revenue Section, and was made Gentleman Awaiting Orders in the Dragon Diagram Hall with acting charge of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 未逾月，得疾，仁宗封藥賜之，使未及門而卒。

translations.literal: Within a month he fell ill. Emperor Renzong sealed medicine and sent it as a gift, but the messenger had not yet reached his door when he died.
translations.idiomatic: Less than a month later he took ill. Emperor Renzong sent sealed medicine as a gift, but the courier had not yet reached his gate when he died.

sentences.zh: 孫冲，字升伯，趙州平棘人。

translations.literal: Sun Chong, styled Shengbo, was a native of Pingji in Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chong, courtesy name Shengbo, came from Pingji in Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，歷古田青陽尉、鹽山麗水主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and successively served as the Qingyang district officer of Gutian and as recorder of Lishui in Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Mingjing degree and served in turn as Qingyang district officer in Gutian and as recorder of Lishui in Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 嘗並喪父母去官，有司循五代故事，必六年乃聽調，冲援古制，以書干宰相，不納。

translations.literal: He once lost both parents at once and left office; the authorities, following Five Dynasties precedent, required six years before permitting reassignment. Chong cited ancient regulations and petitioned the chief minister by letter, but his request was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When both his parents died together he resigned; the authorities, invoking Five Dynasties custom, would not allow him to take a new post for six years. Chong appealed to ancient precedent in a letter to the chief minister, but the appeal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 後舉進士，登甲科。

translations.literal: Later he passed the jinshi examination in the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: He later passed the jinshi in the highest class.

sentences.zh: 授將作監丞，歷通判晉、絳、保州，坐與保州守爭事，降監吉州酒，累遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed as an assistant in the Directorate of Palace Buildings, served as vice-prefect of Jin, Jiang, and Bao prefectures, was demoted to overseer of the Ji Prefecture wine monopoly for clashing with the prefect of Bao, and was repeatedly promoted to Doctor of the Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an assistant in the Directorate of Palace Buildings, served as vice-prefect of Jin, Jiang, and Bao, was reduced to overseer of Ji Prefecture's wine monopoly after a dispute with Bao's prefect, and eventually rose to Doctor of the Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 河決棣州，知天雄軍寇準請徙州治河，命冲往按視。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River broke through at Di Prefecture, Kou Zhun, commander of the Tianxiong army, requested moving the prefectural seat to treat the river. Chong was ordered to go inspect the situation.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yellow River burst its banks at Di Prefecture, Kou Zhun of the Tianxiong command asked to relocate the prefectural seat to manage the river, and Chong was sent to inspect the site.

sentences.zh: 還言：「徙州動民，亦未免治堤，不若塞河為便。」

translations.literal: On returning he said: "Moving the prefectural seat will disturb the people, and one will still need to maintain dikes—it is better to block the river breach."
